articles.title: Christian McCaffrey headlines 9 in-season trades this decade that were big hits, with 9 others that were busts
articles.summary: Every team hopes its splashy in-season trade acquisition leads to a Super Bowl.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks would not have won a Super Bowl without some smart in-season trades for veterans on both sides of the ball.

The 2025 Seahawks are represented well on the list of best in-season trades since 2020. The trade deadline is Tuesday, and there has already been a lot of action . Expect plenty more deals before next week, with teams hoping to acquire that one player who can push them into a Super Bowl.

Here are the nine best and worst in-season trades in the NFL since the 2020 season:

1. Christian McCaffrey, 2022, Panthers to 49ers

This trade was so good for the 49ers, it's hard to remember McCaffrey as a member of the Panthers. The 49ers paid up for McCaffrey, sending draft picks in the second, third, fourth and fifth rounds for a back who at that point was dynamic but had played just 10 games the previous two seasons combined due to injuries. It turned out to be a bargain for the 49ers.

Here's what McCaffrey has done since the trade: 6,347 yards from scrimmage and 56 total touchdowns in 4 1/2 seasons, with NFL Offensive Player of the Year and NFL Comeback Player of the Year awards. McCaffrey has cemented himself as a future Hall of Famer and one of the best running backs ever . San Francisco made one Super Bowl with McCaffrey and is a contender to do it again this season.

The Panthers used those picks to help them get Bryce Young in a big trade, and also a trade up to get edge rusher D.J. Johnson in the third round. Johnson had a half of a sack before he was out of the NFL. It was a heist for San Francisco.

2. Ernest Jones IV, 2024, Titans to Seahawks

Jones had a weird 2024. He was traded from the Rams to the Titans right before the season for a late-round draft pick swap. The Titans had a terrible season and then unloaded Jones to the Seahawks for linebacker Jerome Baker and a fourth-round pick. All Jones has done since then is become one of the NFL's best off-ball linebackers. He has 301 tackles, seven interceptions and four sacks in 33 regular-season games for Seattle. He's a remarkable fit for Mike Macdonald's defense. He was a key component to the Seahawks' Super Bowl championship team. Baker played five games for the Titans and is out of football this season, and the pick became tight end Gunnar Helm, who has 517 career yards over two seasons.

Smith hasn't brought a championship to the Ravens but he has been a stellar performer. In his first three full seasons with Baltimore he was a Pro Bowler each time. The Bears got a second-round pick, used on defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. (before this season Chicago traded Dexter to the Falcons for cornerback Clark Phillips III and a 2027 fifth-round draft pick, and since then Dexter signed a four-year, $78 million extension), a fifth-round pick and linebacker A.J. Klein, who didn't record a stat in two games for Chicago.

Miller played 12 games for the Rams, including playoffs. He had a massive impact in that short time. Miller had five sacks in the regular season and four more in the playoffs, which led all players that postseason. He had two sacks in a Super Bowl win over the Bengals. The Rams might not have won that championship without Miller. The Broncos did well too. They got a second- and third-round pick for Miller. The second-round pick became defensive end Nik Bonitto, one of the league's best pass rushers. A true win-win deal.

5. Leonard Williams, 2023, Giants to Seahawks

The Seahawks sent a second- and fifth-round pick to the Giants for Williams, which was a steep price for a 29-year-old defensive lineman. Williams made Pro Bowls in 2024 and 2025 and has been a leader and perfect fit for one of the NFL's best defenses. Last season, the Seahawks won a Super Bowl with Williams being a huge part of it. The price wasn't so steep after all.

6. Jeffery Simmons, 2026, Titans to Bears

Too soon? Maybe. But it was undeniable that the Bears' defense looked completely different with Simmons in the middle in his debut. The price was heavy, with two first-round picks going to the Titans. But we'll project a bit and say Chicago will be happy to have Simmons, one of the top interior defensive players in the NFL.

7. Montez Sweat, 2023, Commanders to Bears

Funny enough, had the Commanders just used the 40th overall draft pick that the Bears sent them for Sweat, the trade would have looked better. That pick was defensive back Cooper DeJean, who has become a good player … for the Eagles. The Commanders traded down and took cornerback Mike Sainristil and tight end Ben Sinnott. Neither have worked out. Sweat has 24.5 sacks in 48 games for the Bears and with Jeffery Simmons coming aboard this season, is a key part of a good defensive line for a Super Bowl contender.

8. Rashid Shaheed, 2025, Saints to Seahawks

Shaheed has just 351 receiving yards in 16 regular-season games for the Seahawks, since Seattle sent fourth- and fifth-round picks to New Orleans for the big-play receiver. Why is this a positive trade? Because Shaheed made perhaps the biggest play of the Seahawks' Super Bowl run, with a 58-yard punt return with about eight minutes left with Seattle trailing the Rams 30-14 in a Week 16 game. That sparked a huge comeback that led to a Seahawks overtime win, and it was a springboard to a championship. Shaheed also started the playoff run with a 95-yard kickoff return for a touchdown on the opening play of a divisional-round rout of the 49ers. Those big returns were well worth the cost.

9. Kadarius Toney, 2022, Giants to Chiefs

Toney's Chiefs career didn't end great, so you might remember the drops, penalties and controversies and think it was a bad trade. And that's reasonable. But Toney made two enormous plays in a Super Bowl win over the Eagles. Kansas City trailed 27-21 in the fourth quarter when Toney scored a 5-yard touchdown and then had a 65-yard punt return to set up another short touchdown. The Chiefs won 38-35 on a field goal as time expired. Toney might have been a headache overall, but without sending those third- and sixth-round picks to the Giants, do the Chiefs win Super Bowl LVII?

In the moment, this trade didn't seem so bad. The Colts were 7-2 when they traded for Gardner, one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL. The price was huge, sending two first-round draft picks and receiver Adonai Mitchell to New York. But it looked like the Colts were getting an impact player for a playoff push. Since then the Colts are 3-13 and have fired general manager Chris Ballard. Mitchell has dealt with injuries but is coming off a 142-yard game. The Colts' collapse isn't all Gardner's fault, but he has been injured and has not done much for Indianapolis. Meanwhile, the Colts continue to trade players, and their first-round pick next year that will go to the Jets could be in the top five. Meanwhile, it's arguable that Mitchell's value has caught up to Gardner, or at least made it close for a player whom Indianapolis included as a rage throw-in after Mitchell dropped the ball before scoring a touchdown against the Chargers. Given the cost and return on investment, it's probably the most damaging trade on this list.

2. Chase Claypool, 2022, Steelers to Bears

Even in the moment it seemed questionable that the Bears would send what would end up being a high second-round pick to the Steelers for Claypool, who was inconsistent on the field. It ended up being one of the worst trades in the NFL over many years. For the rest of Claypool's career he had 22 catches for 117 yards and one touchdown. Claypool was out of the NFL at age 26. Meanwhile, the pick sent to the Steelers ended up being 32nd overall and was used on Joey Porter Jr., who became one of the league's best young corners (and was traded to the Cowboys for a second- and sixth-round pick this season).

When the Jets traded for Adams, everyone wondered what they were thinking. The trade was made the day after the Jets fell to 2-4. They had already fired head coach Robert Saleh. They still sent a third-round pick to the Raiders for Adams. He played well, with 854 yards, but the Jets predictably went 5-12 and the team released Adams the next offseason due to salary cap reasons. The Raiders didn't exactly put that pick they got to good use. They traded it to Seattle for Geno Smith. And the Seahawks burned that on quarterback Jalen Milroe, who has had no impact.

4. Marshon Lattimore, 2024, Saints to Commanders

Washington traded third-, fourth- and sixth-round picks to the Saints for Lattimore and a fifth-round pick. At the time Lattimore was considered a top cornerback. But the Commanders quickly found that Lattimore was in decline. He did not play well in 11 games with the team, tore his ACL during the 2025 season, was released for salary cap reasons this past offseason and remains unsigned.

5. Jaelan Phillips, 2025, Dolphins to Eagles

Part of the error of this trade was the Eagles seemingly miscalculating the market on Phillips, who was to be a 2026 free agent. The Eagles traded a third-round pick to the Dolphins for Phillips. He played eight games for Philadelphia and had two sacks for a team that faded hard at the end of the season and did not win a playoff game. Phillips then left the Eagles in free agency, signing a four-year, $120 million deal in Carolina. The Eagles didn't expect that, and reacted by trading two third-round picks to the Vikings for Jonathan Greenard, a 29-year-old edge rusher who has two tackles and no sacks this season. Greenard signed a four-year, $98 million extension after the trade. So it can be argued the final cost of the Phillips deal was three third-round picks and $98 million for a total of two sacks from a pair of players.

The Bills thought they were getting a key weapon for Josh Allen when they traded a third- and seventh-round pick to the Browns for Cooper and a sixth. Cooper was almost immediately hurt with a wrist injury and made practically no impact. Cooper had 297 yards and two touchdowns with the Bills, Buffalo lost the AFC championship game to the Chiefs (Cooper had 33 yards in that game) and Cooper never played another down in the NFL after that season. The third-round pick was used by the Browns on quarterback Dillon Gabriel, who hasn't worked out either.

7. Jonathan Mingo, 2024, Panthers to Cowboys

The Cowboys' trade for Mingo was surprising because they sent a fourth-round pick to Carolina for a player who had done very little in the NFL. And Mingo has done even less with the Cowboys. Since that trade two years ago he has nine catches for 101 yards and no touchdowns. The Cowboys might have thought they were outsmarting the rest of the NFL with that deal, but it turns out everyone else was correct in thinking Dallas had just made a mistake.

8. Calvin Ridley, 2022, Falcons to Jaguars

At the time the Jaguars seemed to be buying low on Ridley, who was serving a year-long suspension for betting on NFL games. The trade compensation was conditional and ultimately Jacksonville sent the 79th overall pick of the 2024 draft to the Falcons for Ridley. What the Jaguars got for that was a modest 1,016 yards in one 9-8 season with Ridley, who left for Tennessee as a free agent.

9. Bradley Chubb, 2022, Broncos to Dolphins

It might be harsh to put the Chubb deal on this list. He was productive, with 22 sacks in 41 games. But the Dolphins swung big on a deal to improve their chances of a deep playoff run, and that didn't happen. The Dolphins sent a first-round pick along with a fourth and running back Chase Edmonds to Denver for Chubb and a fifth. The Dolphins didn't win a division title or playoff game after the trade, tore the roster down this past offseason and Chubb's $10.97 dead cap hit is part of the overwhelming overall dead cap hit of more than $188 million for the 2026 Dolphins.

articles.title: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice reportedly files for bankruptcy, citing $3.45 million in debts following fallout from 2024 car crash
articles.summary: Rice reportedly claimed that he owes $2.1 million as a result of multiple civil lawsuits.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice has filed for bankruptcy, according to court filings obtained by multiple outlets. In the filings, Rice reportedly claims that he has more than $3.45 million in debts.

A significant chunk of Rice's debt, per the filing, stems from several lawsuits the receiver has faced over the past year. Rice was sued by multiple victims of a Dallas car crash he was part of in 2024 and was sued in February by an ex-girlfriend who alleged that he physically abused her for more than a year.

Rice, who reportedly filed the claim in the Northern District of Texas bankruptcy court, says that more that $2.1 million of his debts are tied to the lawsuits. The civil suit for the crash was settled in July, with Rice set to pay $1 million (plus lawyers' fees) to the two plaintiffs; the lawsuit with his ex-girlfriend is still awaiting trial.

Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy, which will result in the liquidation and sale of assets to help repay debts, rather than Chapter 13, which would create a payment plan using his regular income.

In the filing, Rice reportedly claimed $677,054 in personal assets, which includes $421,825 in "deferred compensation." Other assets reportedly listed include a Mercedes-Benz worth $53,000, an apartment lease worth $3,500, and $5,000 in NFL jerseys and hats. Rice also placed his Super Bowl LVIII ring, which he valued at $160,000, as collateral, per ESPN .

Rice is in the final year of a four-year rookie deal worth $6,085,657 in total compensation, per Spotrac .

As part of the fallout from the Dallas crash, Rice was sentenced to five years' probation and 30 days in jail in July. He served a six-game suspension from the NFL to start the 2025 season.

Rice served his jail sentence over the summer, calling it "a learning experience and "a reality check" after he returned to Chiefs training camp in August. He has played in five games this season, missing two games last month after suffering a hamstring injury .

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers makes major donation to support U.S. women's flag football ahead of 2028 Olympics
articles.summary: Earlier this year, Aaron Rodgers made headlines with his decision to continue his NFL career with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body: Earlier this year, Aaron Rodgers made headlines with his decision to continue his NFL career with the Pittsburgh Steelers. But the veteran quarterback is now drawing attention for a different reason. The four-time NFL MVP is putting his influence and resources behind women's flag football as the sport prepares for its historic Olympic debut in 2028. Rodgers has reportedly made a donation to USA Football to support the U.S. Women's National Flag Football Team, giving the players another boost as they work towards competing for gold on home soil in Los Angeles.Aaron Rodgers supports U.S. women's flag football with donation ahead of OlympicsRodgers' contribution comes at an important time for women's flag football. The sport is preparing for its first appearance at the 2028 Summer Olympics, where both men's and women's teams will compete for medals.According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the Steelers quarterback is making a donation to USA Football specifically to help the women's national team prepare for the upcoming competition. While the financial details of his contribution have not been disclosed, the gesture highlights the growing interest in a sport that is gaining recognition beyond traditional American football.Flag football offers a different challenge from the NFL game. Players rely on speed, quick decisions, teamwork and sharp passing rather than tackling opponents. That difference makes Olympic preparation especially important, even for athletes who have spent years playing professional football.The United States enters the competition with an impressive record. The men's national team has won five consecutive gold medals at the IFAF Flag Football World Championship, while the women's team has claimed the last three titles.The American women also defeated Mexico 31-18 in the 2024 championship final, underlining their status as one of the strongest teams in the sport.Aaron Rodgers' final NFL season adds another chapter to his legacyRodgers' donation also comes as the 42-year-old prepares for what could be the final chapter of his remarkable NFL career.The quarterback committed to returning to Pittsburgh for the 2026 season after helping the Steelers win the AFC North title and secure a playoff appearance in 2025. He will now look to finish his career with another strong campaign.His achievements already place him among the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history. Rodgers is a four-time NFL MVP, a Super Bowl champion, a Super Bowl MVP and a 10-time Pro Bowler. He has also earned four First-Team All-Pro selections.Meanwhile, the 2028 Olympics could create another major opportunity for American football. The NFL unanimously approved allowing its players to participate in flag football at the Games in 2025, although their involvement remains uncertain.With the 2026 Flag Football World Championship scheduled for August in Germany, Team USA has another important test before Los Angeles. Rodgers' support offers a timely reminder that the sport's growth depends on more than professional stars. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' KC Current get $72 million federal boost for major $800 million riverfront project
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have another reason to be excited about the future of the Kansas City Current.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have another reason to be excited about the future of the Kansas City Current. A major federal investment could soon make reaching their NWSL club's home stadium much easier. The proposed $72 million project aims to remove dangerous railway crossings and create a direct connection between historic neighbourhoods, the Berkley Riverfront and CPKC Stadium. Beyond improving matchday travel, the development could reshape one of Kansas City's fastest-growing areas, bringing new housing, businesses and better transport links. For the Mahomes family and the Current, this could mark an important step in the club's long-term growth.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' KC Current get major boost from $72 million grantThe U.S. Department of Transportation's Federal Railroad Administration has awarded up to $72 million to Port KC to eliminate three railway crossings along Lydia Avenue.The project will replace ground-level crossings with a flyover bridge, allowing vehicles and pedestrians to travel safely above the tracks. The improvement aims to end long traffic delays caused by passing trains while making the riverfront more accessible.Port KC will contribute the remaining 20% of the project's cost. The federal funding will support land acquisition, final design work and construction.For Patrick and Brittany Mahomes, who are part of the ownership group behind the Kansas City Current, the development carries particular importance. Better access to CPKC Stadium could make attending matches and visiting the surrounding entertainment district easier for supporters.Port KC President and CEO Jon Stephens highlighted the wider benefits of the project.“Dangerous and time-consuming rail crossings will be eliminated at Lydia Avenue with the construction of a flyover bridge that will include safe walking paths to allow for increased vehicular and pedestrian connectivity to the Missouri Riverfront,” Port KC President and CEO Jon Stephens said. “This project will also enhance freight rail efficiency and strengthen the movement of goods through Kansas City.”CPKC Stadium development could transform Kansas City's riverfrontThe bridge is part of a much larger vision for the Berkley Riverfront. Port KC and the Kansas City Current have unveiled an $800 million development plan featuring thousands of homes, shops and restaurants..The project also aims to connect Columbus Park with the riverfront, the KC Streetcar extension and nearby businesses. This could turn the stadium area into a more accessible destination throughout the year, rather than a place people visit only on matchdays.Kansas City Mayor Quinton Lucas also welcomed the announcement.“The new Lydia flyover bridge will be another great addition to the Riverfront, linking a larger-capacity CPKC Stadium, thousands of housing units, new restaurants and small businesses, and the streetcar extension with historic neighborhoods in Northeast Kansas City,” Lucas said..KC Current co-owner Chris Long described the bridge as a 'game-changer' for fans and visitors.Planning and design work will begin immediately, but officials have not announced a construction start date.For the Mahomes family and the KC Current, improved transport could strengthen the stadium's connection with the wider community. The $72 million federal boost brings that vision closer, although residents will have to wait for a confirmed construction timeline.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Joe Burrow's painful childhood memories fuel emotional $530,000 effort to save Ohio children from hunger
articles.summary: Last year, Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow used his NFL fame to support a cause that hits close to home.
articles.body: Last year, Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow used his NFL fame to support a cause that hits close to home. The star quarterback joined Ohio Governor Mike DeWine and community leaders at a major fundraising event aimed at tackling childhood hunger. His appearance helped generate record support for Children's Hunger Alliance, raising an impressive $530,000. For Burrow, the cause carried a personal connection. Growing up in Athens County, Ohio, he witnessed the challenges faced by families dealing with poverty and food insecurity. Those early experiences continue to shape his efforts to give back.Joe Burrow helps raise $530,000 at Ohio's Menu of Hope eventThe 30th annual Menu of Hope took place on March 6, 2025, at the Hyatt Regency Ballroom in Columbus, Ohio. The event brought together nearly 800 supporters from the corporate, government and community sectors. Their combined efforts generated a record $530,000 for Children's Hunger Alliance.Burrow was the headline guest at the gathering, where he discussed his journey with the Bengals and the experiences that inspired his charitable work. He also spoke about establishing the Joe Burrow Foundation and his commitment to helping people facing difficult circumstances.Ohio Governor Mike DeWine and First Lady Fran DeWine also addressed the audience, highlighting the importance of proper nutrition for children. Their presence added further support to an initiative focused on making healthy food accessible to young people across the state.The event also marked Children's Hunger Alliance's 55th anniversary, making the fundraising milestone even more meaningful.Joe Burrow's childhood experiences inspire his fight against hungerBurrow's connection to childhood hunger goes beyond his public profile as an NFL quarterback. His upbringing in Athens County gave him an understanding of the struggles that many families experience when putting food on the table.That personal connection made his involvement in Menu of Hope particularly significant. Through the Joe Burrow Foundation and his participation in community initiatives, the quarterback continues to use his success to support people who need assistance.The scale of the problem in Ohio remains concerning. Nearly one in five children in the state experiences food insecurity, according to Children's Hunger Alliance.The organisation's work has already made a considerable difference. In 2024, it provided nearly 11 million nutritious meals to more than 161,000 children across Ohio through partnerships with over 1,800 sites in 76 counties.Its programmes cover school breakfasts, after-school meals, weekend food support and summer nutrition assistance.The $530,000 raised at Menu of Hope will help strengthen these efforts and support the organisation's mission. For Burrow, the event offered another opportunity to turn a personal experience into something meaningful for thousands of children growing up in circumstances he understands.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Going to have a problem in the future": Travis Kelce's $5.35 million mansion faces potential environmental disaster as neighbours raise serious concerns
articles.summary: Travis Kelce wanted his $5.35 million Ohio mansion to become a private escape from the spotlight.
articles.body: Travis Kelce wanted his $5.35 million Ohio mansion to become a private escape from the spotlight. Instead, his plans to reshape the historic estate have sparked growing tension in Bratenahl. What should have been a peaceful lakeside retreat is now facing questions about the surrounding environment, ageing infrastructure and the risks of changing an established residential landscape. Neighbours fear that introducing extensive greenery and altering the property's surroundings could trigger problems that extend well beyond the mansion's boundaries. The concerns have put the couple's renovation plans under fresh scrutiny.Travis Kelce face growing environmental concerns over their Ohio mansionThe biggest concern among residents centres on the property's landscaping plans. Adding rows of evergreen trees might improve privacy, but neighbours worry that the changes could have consequences for the natural surroundings.Katherine Bolton, who has lived next to the property for more than 30 years, raised concerns about planting trees close to underground infrastructure. She told the Bratenahl Architectural Review Board that the shared sewer line dates back approximately 115 years.Her warning highlighted a problem that can develop slowly before becoming expensive to fix."When you plant that many trees from a short distance from a sewer line, you're going to have a problem in the future," Bolton said, according to Cleveland 19.She also revealed that she had received a $75,000 estimate for lining the ageing pipe to protect it against possible root intrusion.The concern is not simply about the trees themselves. Root growth can affect underground structures, while changes to established vegetation can also influence the local environment. However, no future damage has been confirmed.Travis Kelce's $7,500 repair fails to settle Ohio mansion disputeKelce and Swift's representatives have already taken steps to address some of the complaints. Property manager Patrick Hyland told officials that the couple had spent $7,500 repairing a damaged section of the shared sewer line. Workers also cleaned the pipe to reduce the risk of further complications.However, the landscaping dispute continues.The proposed security fence has also changed following objections. The original eight-foot design was reduced to six feet and moved inside the property boundary. Additional gates were included to maintain access and address residents' concerns.Neighbour Chuck Bauernschmidt also questioned the removal of existing vegetation and raised concerns about wildlife."I live here, been here for 47 years. I take offense when we start knocking trees down," he said.Meanwhile, officials questioned whether the proposed rear-yard trees would exceed Bratenahl's 10-foot height restriction.The board approved the front landscaping, but the rear plans remained unresolved. A further review was scheduled for November 10.For Kelce and Swift, the challenge is becoming bigger than improving privacy. Their 21,000-square-foot estate, featuring eight bedrooms and 11 bathrooms, may offer luxury and seclusion, but its surroundings demand careful planning. Until residents and officials reach an agreement, their dream Ohio retreat will remain caught in an increasingly complicated neighbourhood dispute.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chiefs Receiver Rashee Rice Files for Bankruptcy Over Debts From Crash, Alleged Assault
articles.summary: DALLAS (AP) — Kansas City Chiefs receiver Rashee Rice has filed for bankruptcy, claiming $3.5 million in debts, most of it connected to civil ligitation involving his high-speed crash in Texas and allegations of assault by a former girlfriend.
articles.body:
DALLAS (AP) — Kansas City Chiefs receiver Rashee Rice has filed for bankruptcy, claiming $3.5 million in debts, most of it connected to civil ligitation involving his high-speed crash in Texas and allegations of assault by a former girlfriend.

The filing made Wednesday in Texas lists $677,054 in personal assets, including $421,825 in what is listed as deferred compensation. Rice is in the final year of a four-year rookie contract with a total value of $6.5 million and a 2026 base salary of $1.6 million.

Rice's largest debtor is owed $979,837 as part of a settlement for his role in the 2024 crash in Dallas that left multiple people injured and led to a six-game suspension by the NFL .

The 26-year-old is disputing potential debts in ongoing civil cases, including a combined $700,000 in lawsuits filed by crash victims and another $200,000 from the ex-girlfriend who alleged he assaulted her multiple times from 2023-25. The league did not punish Rice over the assault allegations.

Rice was was sentenced to 30 days in jail and five years' probation over the crash. He pleaded guilty to third-degree felony charges of collision involving serious bodily injury and racing on a highway causing bodily injury.

Rice served another 30 days in jail this year for violating his probation by testing positive for marijuana.

The former SMU player has 20 catches for 243 yards and two touchdowns this season. Rice had 938 yards receiving and seven touchdowns as a rookie in 2023, when the Chiefs won the Super Bowl.

articles.title: Ravens' Plans, Timeline for Jacoby Brissett Revealed in Latest NFL Rumors After Cardinals Trade
articles.summary: Jacoby Brissett won't be on the Baltimore Ravens in time to start Thursday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars with Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) injured, but the plan is reportedly for him to take the field in Week 10.
articles.body:
Jacoby Brissett won't be on the Baltimore Ravens in time to start Thursday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars with Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) injured, but the plan is reportedly for him to take the field in Week 10.

"That is the expectation," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported when asked if Brissett will start against the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 16.

His update comes after he and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the Ravens "are finalizing a trade" to acquire the veteran quarterback from the Arizona Cardinals in a move that is "expected to be completed this weekend."

Baltimore came into the season with realistic Super Bowl expectations in large part because of Jackson's presence under center, but now it is in scramble mode following the injuries to its top-two quarterbacks.

Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start Thursday's game after seeing some action in the team's most recent loss to the Buffalo Bills.

He went 10-of-21 for 91 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception in defeat.

As for Brissett, he was benched in the Cardinals' overtime win over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. Gardner Minshew II entered the game and overcame a 14-point deficit in the fourth quarter with touchdown passes to Tyler Allgeier, Trey McBride and Michael Wilson.

With Minshew and rookie Carson Beck on the roster, Brissett became expendable.

Now it seems like the veteran will be tasked with leading the Ravens back into the AFC playoff picture. They enter Thursday's game with three straight losses and a 4-4 record, which has them in last place in the AFC North.

There is plenty of talent on the offense with Derrick Henry, Zay Flowers and Mark Andrews, among others, but the quarterback play will ultimately determine the team's ceiling the rest of the season.

And it seems like that will be Brissett by Baltimore's next game.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill donated 200 Chick-fil-A sandwiches to hospital workers in heartwarming gesture
articles.summary: In 2020, when the COVID-19 pandemic brought everyday life to a standstill, healthcare workers faced an extraordinary challenge.
articles.body: In 2020, when the COVID-19 pandemic brought everyday life to a standstill, healthcare workers faced an extraordinary challenge. While hospitals struggled to care for patients, former Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyreek Hill found a way to show his appreciation for those working on the front lines. The NFL star stepped away from the football field and headed to a Kansas City hospital with an important delivery. His gesture was simple but meaningful, offering a reminder that even small acts of kindness can make a difference during difficult times.Tyreek Hill donated 200 meals to Kansas City hospital workers in 2020On May 7, 2020, Hill visited Saint Luke's North Hospital in Kansas City, Missouri, to deliver meals to doctors, nurses and other essential employees.The initiative was organised through the Tyreek Hill Foundation in partnership with Chick-fil-A. Together, they provided approximately 200 sandwiches for hospital staff members who were working long hours amid the coronavirus crisis.Hill did more than simply arrange the donation. He personally distributed the food across different hospital departments, making sure employees received their meals. He wore a face mask and gloves during the visit, while his mother and grandmother accompanied him.The visit offered a glimpse of the values that shaped Hill's beyond professional football. Hill credited his family for teaching him the importance of sharing his success and helping others whenever possible.“Being on this platform means a lot to me. I am always doing my best to give back. My family taught me that and I want to teach my kids the same thing,” Hill said.His message reflected a broader sense of responsibility among athletes during the pandemic. With millions of people following NFL stars, Hill understood that his influence could extend beyond touchdowns and record-breaking performances.Tyreek Hill compared healthcare workers' efforts to winning the Super BowlHill also spoke about the dedication he witnessed inside the hospital. The wide receiver recognised that healthcare professionals were facing a different kind of battle, one that required courage, patience and constant commitment.“They are out here grinding, man,” the 26-year-old remarked. “I can’t do nothing but just be thankful for them. The same way I’m grinding on the field, they’re grinding right here in their department. They are winning their own Super Bowl.”The comparison captured the spirit of his visit. While NFL players compete for championships, medical professionals were fighting to protect lives during an unprecedented health crisis.Hill's foundation also planned another meal giveaway to continue supporting healthcare workers.Looking back, the donation remains a memorable example of Tyreek Hill using his platform for something beyond football. His visit was not about headlines or recognition. It was about acknowledging the people who kept showing up when their communities needed them most.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld gave Buffalo Bills players and their partners a Halloween party to remember, but the celebrations have drawn attention for another reason. Pictures and videos from their private gathering have surfaced online, offering a look at the couple's elaborate Alice in Wonderland theme. Steinfeld has also shared a rare glimpse of Allen with their daughter, Harper Haize, through her Beau Society newsletter. The two developments have put the family's Halloween celebrations in focus, particularly as the couple continues to keep their baby away from regular public attention.Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld turn Halloween into an Alice in Wonderland partyThe couple hosted the Bills' annual Halloween gathering on Monday, November 2, a day after Buffalo's 36-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. Rather than choosing separate costumes, Allen and Steinfeld built the evening around a shared theme, calling it "Allen's in Wonderland."The entrance set the tone before guests even reached the main party area. A giant clock carried the event's name, followed by a long black-and-white tunnel. Inside, glowing letters spelling "We're all mad here" added another familiar detail from Lewis Carroll's story.Steinfeld dressed as the Queen of Hearts in a black outfit decorated with red roses, complete with a cape and crown. Allen matched her as the King of Hearts. Their costumes were among the most striking looks of the night, but the Bills players and their partners also joined in.Wide receiver DJ Moore and his wife, Raven Moore, chose Violet Beauregarde and Augustus Gloop from Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. Offensive tackle Dion Dawkins and his fiancée, Diayaana, went with Marge Simpson and Sideshow Bob. Raven Moore helped bring the private celebration into public view by sharing photographs from the gathering on Instagram.Steinfeld later discussed the planning behind the event in her Beau Society newsletter. She said she had loved the "Allen’s in Wonderland" idea and wanted to use it the previous year, but the couple were not married then. "Getting back into hosting was a blast," she added, explaining that local business owners helped turn her mood board into reality.Harper's appearance gives fans another glimpse into family lifeThe party was not the only reason Steinfeld's latest updates attracted attention. Her newsletter also offered a personal look at Allen spending time with their daughter, Harper. The actress described watching the baby smile and laugh with her father as one of the everyday moments that brings her happiness."Watching my baby girl smile and laugh with her dad, my incredible husband."That small detail offered something different from the elaborate party pictures. Allen and Steinfeld have generally kept Harper out of the public eye, so even a limited glimpse of the quarterback with his daughter drew interest. The couple welcomed Harper in April 2026, and this Halloween marked their first celebration as parents.Harper also had her own place in the Wonderland theme. Images from the celebrations showed her dressed in a blue Alice-inspired outfit, giving the family event a fitting finishing touch. Steinfeld has also revealed that Harper tried several other Halloween looks, including a bat, a Cabbage Patch doll and a Highland cow, which Allen picked.For a couple whose professional lives attract constant attention, the distinction is clear. They are happy to share the work that went into a large celebration, but their daughter's everyday life remains largely theirs to protect. articles.title: Travis Hunter Shares Highlight Video of Brother Trayvis' HSFB Game with 2 TDs, 100+ Yards
articles.summary: After helping the Jacksonville Jaguars get off to an early AFC South lead, two-way star Travis Hunter took some time to support his family during the team's Week 7 bye.
articles.body:
After helping the Jacksonville Jaguars get off to an early AFC South lead, two-way star Travis Hunter took some time to support his family during the team's Week 7 bye.

Hunter shared a video on Thursday showing him attend a high school football game in Georgia to cheer on his younger brother, Trayvis Hunter.

Trayvis, a junior at Effingham County High School in Springfield, Ga., compiled over 100 receiving yards and two touchdowns during a 42-21 victory against Grovetown. The 5-foot-7 wide receiver has already received scholarship offers from Georgia Southern and Georgia State, according to Savannah Morning News .

Collins Hill High School head coach Drew Swick, who formerly coached both of the Hunter brothers, spoke glowingly about Trayvis during an interview with DNVR Sports in 2024.

"[Trayvis will] be a little bit shorter than Travis," Swick said. "He's a slot receiver and also plays corner and safety for us and also does returning. He's an unbelievable athlete, you talk to him he wants to be his own person. He's just as good as Travis as a freshman, we didn't have him start as a freshman like Travis but if we didn't have as much skill as we've got he probably would be up there and able to start earlier. He's an unbelievable kid with high academics and is well-respected in the building and the community."

During his collegiate career, the elder Hunter became the first player to play both offense and defense since NFL Hall of Famer Charles Woodson. The 2024 Heisman Trophy winner was selected with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, and he has helped transform Jacksonville into a Super Bowl contender.

The Jaguars are set to face the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night Football with hopes of improving to a 6-2 record. Hunter has improved as a defensive player in his second season. After reeling in a pair of interceptions before Jacksonville's bye, he'll have another opportunity to force turnovers against a Baltimore team that's starting their third-string quarterback.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk's Agent Updates Plans for 49ers WR amid NFL Reinstatement Attempt
articles.summary: Brandon Aiyuk is planning to return to the San Francisco 49ers Friday after a yearslong split from the team.
articles.body:
Brandon Aiyuk is planning to return to the San Francisco 49ers Friday after a yearslong split from the team.

Agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter Aiyuk plans to report to the 49ers Friday afternoon.

"We will be there tomorrow at 3pm to meet with the team at the facility," Rosenhaus told Schefter. "We will put our best foot forward and go from there."

There are complications with the receiver's potential return. As Tom Pelissero of The Ringer explained, Aiyuk could owe the 49ers $13 million:

It hasn't stopped his plans to return to this point. Rosenhaus told Schefter Thursday Aiyuk is healthy and "ready to get back on the field."

Aiyuk is under contract through the 2028 season but has not seen NFL action since October 2024.

He has repeatedly called for the 49ers to release him from his contract in social media posts over the past year.

Rosenhaus also told Schefter he had filed the paperwork to apply for Aiyuk's reinstatement.

The 49ers have been split for at least a year from Aiyuk, who suffered his season-ending right knee injury in October 2024.

Aiyuk remained sidelined for the start of the 2025 season. The Athletic's Dianna Russini and Michael Silver reported in November the 49ers had voided Aiyuk's guarantees for 2026 because Aiyuk had "failed to attend meetings and declined to participate in other team activities in recent months."

The wide receiver said in a June Instagram video the Niners had also voided his guarantees for the 2027 season.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Wednesday he had "moved on mentally" from Aiyuk's situation.

When asked Thursday on KNBR's Dirty Work if Aiyuk could do anything to change that, Shanahan said, "Not that I could think of... There's no absolutes, and I'll talk to anybody."

Shanahan added there was no Friday meeting currently scheduled between him or his team and Aiyuk.

General manager John Lynch said the same day on KNBR's Murph & Marcus show "everything's possible" regarding Aiyuk.

"Number one, we've got a 6-1 football team that we think's really got a shot at this thing this year, so our focus is going to remain on this team," Lynch said.

Lynch continued, "I will say this. We've worked with Drew a lot. Drew is a good guy to deal with... We'll see how this thing goes. I'll leave it at that."

49ers tight end George Kittle said Thursday he would "plead the fifth" about whether he felt Aiyuk would ultimately get into the Niners facility (h/t 49ers on SI's Grant Cohn).

San Francisco has ultimately paid Aiyuk $48.1 million for just seven games since he signed his extension in August 2024.

The 49ers would have to take on $12.4 million in dead cap this season and $19.3 million in dead cap next season in order to release the remainder of that contract, per Spotrac's Mike Ginnitti .

The Niners will get at least $4.99 million back as a salary cap credit next season, and could get more money back in the future by recouping some of Aiyuk's previous bonuses, Ginnitti noted. The 49ers currently have $32.1 million in 2026 cap space, per Spotrac .

The San Francisco Standard 's David Lombardi reported the 49ers could also require Aiyuk to pass a physical and place him on injured reserve if he doesn't pass.

That would mean the 49ers wouldn't have to give up a roster spot and would owe Aiyuk around $715,000 in prorated salary, Lombardi reported.

The 49ers are currently preparing for a Sunday matchup against the visiting Las Vegas Raiders. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET in Santa Clara.

articles.title: NFL Trade Rumors: Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb reject George Pickens trade talk as Cowboys face major decision
articles.summary: George Pickens has found himself at the centre of growing trade speculation, but two of the Dallas Cowboys' biggest stars are not ready to see him leave.
articles.body: George Pickens has found himself at the centre of growing trade speculation, but two of the Dallas Cowboys' biggest stars are not ready to see him leave. With the November 10 NFL trade deadline approaching, questions about his future have started gaining attention. However, quarterback Dak Prescott and fellow wide receiver CeeDee Lamb have made their positions clear. Both believe Pickens deserves a long-term future in Dallas rather than an unexpected exit. Their public support comes at a difficult time for the Cowboys, who have lost consecutive games after an encouraging 5-0 start to the 2026 season.Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb reject George Pickens trade rumoursPickens is playing the 2026 season under the franchise tag, making his long-term future an important subject for Dallas. The 25-year-old could become eligible for an extension during the 2027 offseason, but recent developments have raised questions about whether the Cowboys will keep him.Prescott dismissed the growing speculation when reporters asked about suggestions that Dallas should trade its receiver."People say a lot of things I don't believe, so I'm not listening to that one, either," Prescott said Thursday.Lamb also questioned why the Cowboys would consider moving on from a player who has helped improve the team's passing attack."I don't know why that's a thing," Lamb said Thursday of Pickens' trade talks. "C'mon man. Everything that I have been able to accomplish has been because of him and what he's done the year before. Vice versa with everything that I've accomplished the year prior to that. He exposed them [opposing defenses]. Just kind of taking what the defense is giving us, and I feel like that goes hand in hand with why I'm able to do what I'm doing at a great pace."The numbers explain Lamb's appreciation. He has recorded 60 catches for 709 yards and six touchdowns this season. Pickens, meanwhile, entered the campaign following a 1,429-yard season in 2025.Brian Schottenheimer's George Pickens criticism fuels Cowboys trade speculationMuch of the discussion began after Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer criticised Pickens' run blocking following a 23-13 defeat against Green Bay.The Cowboys managed only 48 rushing yards in that game, their lowest total of the season. Pickens' reduced involvement since Week 7 has added to the questions.Lamb has played 106 offensive snaps over the last two games, compared with 79 for Pickens and 98 for Ryan Flournoy. Pickens has also dealt with hamstring and shoulder problems, although his latest injury report listed only the hamstring issue.Prescott defended his teammate's attitude and commitment."George is a great teammate," Prescott said. "And I say that in the sense of, he's gonna do whatever is asked, he's going to do whatever is called. If it's to go block, if it's to just go run a guy off, he's going to do that. He believes in just doing the right thing, and the ball will come his way at times. And so, that's not on George."Lamb also wants Pickens to remain confident."Just when his time comes, I know that he is going to be ready," Lamb said. "That's the only conversation that we have. When that moment comes, you can't really go off of what just happened because if that's the case, you're going to drive yourself into a ditch to be honest. You have to move on, be grown about the situation, come to practice ready to work again and have that same mentality that you had before the game. Remember how you felt. Use that as fuel."Prescott suggested that getting Pickens involved earlier could help revive his production.With the Indianapolis Colts next on the schedule and the November 10 trade deadline approaching, Dallas faces an important decision. For now, its quarterback and leading receiver appear firmly behind keeping Pickens in a Cowboys uniform.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Dak Prescott Praises Cowboys' Mental Health Resources on Anniversary of Marshawn Kneeland's Death
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott praised the team's Huddle 94 program, a new facet of the team's mental health resources, ahead of the one-year anniversary of Marshawn Kneeland's death on Friday.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott praised the team's Huddle 94 program, a new facet of the team's mental health resources, ahead of the one-year anniversary of Marshawn Kneeland's death on Friday.

"I think the team—I know the Cowboys, [team mental health clinician Dr. Heather Twedell], they've done a great job of putting something together, Huddle94, and allowing us to create conversations," Prescott told reporters . "[They allow us] to get together in smaller groups that talk about life and talk about things that are stressors to us that may have—if it was something that we had then, it may have helped Marshawn. It may have been something that would have been a resource for him to prevent what happened. So I'm just trying to honor him by creating those conversations, and by creating that group."

Per ESPN's Todd Archer , the Huddle 94 program includes "player-led roundtable discussions that are designed to add to the culture of the players' brotherhood, the to connection of the players and have conversations about the challenges they face on and off the field."

Kneeland played two seasons with the Cowboys (2024-25). On Nov. 6, 2025, he evaded officers during a traffic pursuit before crashing his car. He died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound and had reportedly expressed suicidal ideations in his past. Following his death he was diagnosed with Stage 1 chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE).

One year later, the memory of Kneeland and what he meant to the players and organization hasn't faded.

"Mental health, just in general, I feel like it's kind of blindly being ignored," wideout CeeDee Lamb noted. "I feel like they see us as figures more so than people, and icons of some sort to some people. ... That was the first teammate in my life that I've actually lost. [You can't] really say that it's something you can really get over because you know that there's a family here and there's a mom crying and there's brothers and wives and everybody involved that's still grieving. So, for us, we got to keep him in our prayers. We do everything we can just to kind of honor him and do everything as far as something that I know he would do as far as come out, practice hard, compete."

articles.title: Eagles' QB Joe Milton Talks Preparation Ahead of 1st NFL Start vs. Giants Amid Jalen Hurts Injury
articles.summary: Joe Milton III will make his first NFL start on Sunday against the New York Giants as the floundering Philadelphia Eagles try to end a six-game losing streak.
articles.body:
Joe Milton III will make his first NFL start on Sunday against the New York Giants as the floundering Philadelphia Eagles try to end a six-game losing streak.

For Milton, staying ready for such a moment was a key part of his preparations throughout the season.

"You never know what can happen in NFL. That's kind of how I took it. Yes, I was on the practice squad, and I was just preparing for any moment that presents itself," he told reporters . "Still, when I was at Dallas on the practice squad, I was just pretty much going through the plays, going through the week like I was a starter or like I was playing, and just being ready. And that's what the NFL is about: Just being ready when your name is called and just preparing for those moments. And I've been preparing and still preparing for the week."

Milton will be the fourth quarterback Philly has used this season behind starter Jalen Hurts and backups Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee. But while those quarterbacks were with the team during training camp, the Birds signed Milton off the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad in mid-October.

And now it's his moment in the spotlight. The possibility that Milton has been preparing for has arrived.

articles.title: Derrick Henry Passes LaDainian Tomlinson in Career Rushing Yards, Who's Next on NFL's All-Time List?
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens star running back Derrick Henry climbed the NFL's all-time rushing leaderboard during a matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens star running back Derrick Henry climbed the NFL's all-time rushing leaderboard during a matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night.

Henry picked up the 13,685th rushing yard of his career in the first half of the game, moving above LaDainian Tomlinson for the No. 7 spot on the league's all-time rushing list.

Henry now sits behind Curtis Martin at No. 6, as Martin amassed 14,101 yards on the ground throughout his career. Adrian Peterson also holds the No. 5 spot on the NFL's all-time leaderboard with 14,918 yards.

Here's a look at the top eight players on the NFL's career rushing list:

While Henry has moved above plenty of players on the league's all-time leaderboard, his latest accomplishment was particularly significant considering who he passed.

The 32-year-old looked up to Tomlinson when he was growing up and had a poster as well as a bobblehead of the former Chargers star, per Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic.

Henry has cemented his status among the top running backs in NFL history, rushing for at least 1,500 yards in five separate seasons of his career. This includes a 2020 campaign in which he amassed a league-leading 2,027 rush yards.

The six-time Pro Bowler owns a career average of 84.8 yards per game on the ground, while his 130 rushing touchdowns are the third-most in NFL history.

Henry has remained a key piece of Baltimore's offense this year, as he tallied 632 rushing yards and eight touchdowns across his first eight appearances of the season.

articles.title: New Lamar Jackson Rumors Reveal Ravens Are Willing to Give QB Largest Contact in NFL History
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens plan to revisit extension talks with Lamar Jackson in the offseason, and those negotiations could ultimately be very fruitful for the star quarterback.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens plan to revisit extension talks with Lamar Jackson in the offseason, and those negotiations could ultimately be very fruitful for the star quarterback.

According to NFL on Prime's James Palmer, "For the last two years the Ravens have been trying to get a long-term contract done with Jackson, and they keep pushing money down the road. Which is why we're at $84 million in terms of a cap hit in 2027. They'd like this offseason—because they won't negotiate during the [NFL season] with one another—to get a long-term contract done, and I'm told the Ravens are willing to have Jackson be the highest-paid player in NFL history. Now Jackson has a no-trade clause, he has a no-franchise-tag clause, and if he would like he could be a full-blown free agent after the 2027 season at the age of 31."

Jackson, 29, injured his thumb on the first play of Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bill after he had missed the previous three games with a high left ankle sprain. The Ravens placed him on injured reserve this week, meaning he will miss a minimum of four games (and potentially more).

Whether Jackson returns may ultimately come down to whether the Ravens have a legitimate chance to make the playoffs. That's very much in question after his backup, Tyler Huntley, was also placed on injured reserve and reportedly suffered a season-ending turf toe injury.

The Ravens started undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano and reportedly have a trade in place with the Arizona Cardinals to acquire veteran Jacoby Brissett. Baltimore came into Thursday's matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars holding a 4-4 record.

While injuries have become a persistent storyline for Jackson during his career, when healthy he's one of the most dynamic players in the sport, as evidenced by his two MVP awards, three first-team All-Pro selections and four Pro Bowl bids. If the Ravens indeed make him the highest-paid player in the history of the sport, nobody will bat an eye.

That distinction currently belongs to Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes and his eight-year, $504.7 million renegotiated deal. Unless Jackson desperately wants to become a free agent, it would be hard to turn down that sort of money, though how the deal is structured and how much guaranteed money it includes will certainly impact negotiations.

articles.title: Rashee Rice's $3.45 million debt takes an unexpected turn as Chiefs star lists his $160,000 Super Bowl ring in bankruptcy filing
articles.summary: Rashee Rice has a Super Bowl ring, an NFL career and a growing list of financial problems.
articles.body: Rashee Rice has a Super Bowl ring, an NFL career and a growing list of financial problems. The Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver has now filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy, reporting more than $3.45 million in debt against just $677,054 in assets. His November 4 filing in federal court also reveals something few would expect from a Super Bowl champion: the ring he won with Kansas City is among the valuables listed in his financial records.And that is only part of the story. A large chunk of Rice's debt comes from legal disputes that have followed him since a serious car crash in 2024. With another lawsuit on his record and his rookie contract nearing its end, the 26-year-old has plenty to sort out away from football. Rashee Rice's Super Bowl LVIII ring appears on his $3.45 million bankruptcy listAccording to ESPN reporters Nate Taylor and Michael Rothstein, Rice owes more than $3.45 million, with over $2.1 million connected to civil lawsuits. His reported assets, meanwhile, stand at $677,054.The asset list includes a 2023 Mercedes-Benz valued at $53,800, deferred compensation worth $421,825, NFL jerseys and hats worth $5,000, and his Super Bowl LVIII ring, which he valued at $160,000. He also listed an apartment lease worth $3,500.The financial trouble largely traces back to March 30, 2024. Rice was driving a Lamborghini Urus at 119 mph on a Dallas highway when he lost control and triggered a crash involving four other vehicles. Several people suffered injuries.One of the victims, Kathryn Kuykendall, later reached a $1 million civil settlement with Rice in April 2025. However, the payment did not arrive as expected.In July 2025, Kuykendall's attorney, Marc Lenahan, told NBC DFW that Rice had no money available when the first payment came due. The lawyer described the situation bluntly, saying there was "Nil" in the receiver's bank account.Rice also pleaded guilty to two third-degree felony charges connected to the crash in July 2025. He received five years of probation and a 30-day jail sentence.Then came another legal headache. In February 2026, his former girlfriend, Dacoda Jones, filed a lawsuit accusing Rice of assaulting her on multiple occasions. She alleged that the incidents left her with bruises and other injuries. Jones sought $1 million in damages. These are allegations in a civil lawsuit, not established findings of guilt.Rice's Chapter 7 filing lists $39,241 in non-exempt assets. The process allows eligible assets to go toward creditors, although the bankruptcy court will determine how the case proceeds. Chiefs star has more than money to worry about as rookie deal nears its endRice's financial problems come at a difficult point in his football career. Kansas City drafted him in the second round in 2023, and he signed a four-year rookie contract worth approximately $6.5 million.His 2026 base salary stands at around $1.6 million. The deal also puts him close to a major career decision, with a potential extension still unresolved.On the field, Rice has not had the season he would have wanted. Through five appearances in 2026, he has recorded 20 catches for 243 yards. Hamstring and knee issues have also limited his participation in practice.That is a far cry from his promising start in Kansas City. Rice finished his rookie season with 938 receiving yards and seven touchdowns before helping the Chiefs beat the San Francisco 49ers in Super Bowl LVIII in February 2024.But the crash and its legal fallout have interrupted his progress. He missed the first six games of the 2025 season because of his NFL suspension, while his probation-related jail sentence added another setback in 2026.Now, Rice has to deal with a bankruptcy case while trying to secure his place in Kansas City. His Super Bowl ring remains a reminder of what he achieved with the Chiefs. His latest court filing, however, shows just how complicated life away from the field has become.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk to return to 49ers' facility Friday afternoon, reportedly discussing forfeiture of $13 million bonus
articles.summary: Aiyuk's return to San Francisco will hopefully resolve a year-long saga.
articles.body:
Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk's attempt at an NFL comeback is underway — though it's not entirely clear if or when he'll be able to pull it off.

More than two years after his last NFL snap, Aiyuk is pushing to make his way back, starting by hiring agent Drew Rosenhaus this week. Next up will be trying to make nice with the San Francisco 49ers, resolving a yearlong saga in order to let Aiyuk return to the field.

Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter that he and Aiyuk will meet with the team at the 49ers' facility at 3 p.m. on Friday. "We will put our best foot forward and go from there," Rosenhaus told Schefter.

A potential wrinkle in that plan, though, is that Aiyuk owes the team around $13 million in bonus forfeiture as a result of the saga, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero . The NFL Management Council and NFL Players Association are involved in trying to find a resolution, which could include an agreement to pay the money back, or potential arbitration, per Pelissero.

Aiyuk missed the entire 2025 season with ACL and MCL tears sustained in October 2024. But the real drama began last November, as the 49ers voided the receiver's 2026 contract guarantees after Aiyuk's relationship with the team became increasingly strained when he failed to show up for team rehab sessions and couldn't be reached for contact. In January, San Francisco general manager John Lynch said that Aiyuk had played his last snap with the Niners .

In June, Aiyuk continued to publicly ask the team to cut him so he could sign somewhere else, specifically the Washington Commanders. But that wasn't going to be possible until he was reinstated from the the reserve/left squad, where he landed because he failed to show up for mandatory team activities, including training camp.

In a video, the receiver said that he would never step foot in the 49ers' facility again; he also claimed that he had fired his agent.

Now, with Rosenhaus leading Aiyuk's negotiations, the receiver will hope to finally get his new start elsewhere, assuming the 49ers trade or cut him.

articles.title: Will Arch Manning, Dante Moore and other QB prospect questions influence NFL trade deadline?
articles.summary: In April, teams were wary of trading away 2027 picks due to the buzz around the class, specifically quarterbacks. If the hype has dimmed, are those picks mor...
articles.body:
As Tuesday's NFL trade deadline draws closer, front offices at all 32 teams are asking themselves: How much do we value our coming draft picks?

And how does that value compare to our assessment of this year's trade candidates ?

The question circulates every year. But with a 2027 NFL Draft class that was strongly heralded in the spring, the calculus feels different.

"Last year, the '27 draft was looming over the '26 draft far more than usual," said a league source with a long history of evaluating the NFL Draft and its quarterback landscape, speaking on condition of anonymity in order to speak freely. "And it has not been a stellar year."

In particular, the first half of the 2026 college football season has not raised the NFL's excitement level about the quarterback class that awaits. Fair or not, that buzz tends to influence the perception of the entire class.

So while talent evaluations between now and April could still shift, it's worth asking: Will a shift in perception of the coming quarterback class influence the NFL trade deadline next week?

In April, teams were wary of trading away 2027 picks due to the buzz around the class, which stemmed largely from buzz around the crop of potential first-round quarterbacks. If the hype has dimmed, are those picks more for sale?

Like most trends in the NFL, the philosophy will differ from team to team. But conversations with league and team voices acknowledge that some draft-eligible players are losing their shine, and some teams could parlay that belief into feeling emboldened at the deadline to acquire players at positions they may not feel the draft is guaranteed to deliver.

Information on draft prospects is incomplete by early November. But one high-ranking AFC executive said they could already get a general sense of the deeper and shallower areas of the draft even if individual evaluations remain unfinished.

"You have all the information, you have general medical history and then you have early background and you can kind of form [opinions]," one high-ranking AFC executive told Yahoo Sports. "You can get close enough to where it's like, 'OK, it's deep. We can solve that in the draft.' Or you're blending with the draft from free agency where it's like [a position] is weaker than other years based on our information [so] it probably makes sense to make this move because between now and the draft, we probably can't solve it the way we want to solve it if we don't do this.

"You're trying to use all that information to piece together the plan."

What information will teams across the league be piecing together? Here's what Yahoo Sports is hearing.

As QB evaluations swirl, do 'people just keep overcorrecting'?

Conversations with executives and evaluators across six different teams offered a mosaic of opinions.

Evaluators from two AFC teams and a high-ranking executive from an NFC team each confirmed they do not view the 2027 NFL Draft as highly now as they did this summer. Each said that reflected their current evaluations of the quarterback class.

"I was part of [the hype], too," one AFC evaluator said. "I got caught up, probably told a bunch of people how this is going to be one of the best draft classes in a long time and it's turning out [not] to be. … There's some good players and there's some really good players at the top, like [Ohio State receiver] Jeremiah Smith. There's a few other players that are really, really talented, but they have a lot of baggage. …

"But this draft isn't turning out to be as deep and as loaded as I anticipated and hoped."

The evaluator from the other AFC team said they believe that 75-80% of draft classes are similarly talented, but perceptions of elite players at premium positions — quarterback, receiver, edge rusher and offensive tackle — disproportionately shift perceptions of each draft. This year, the evaluator saw a dip in receiver, edge and quarterback certainty.

"If that's the case, it's worth buying a player that you can get control on rather than waiting and guessing at the draft," an NFC executive said. "I do think that's part of the Texans' thesis with Marvin Harrison ."

Quarterback questions from evaluators rage: Is Mississippi's 6-foot Trinidad Chambliss big enough for the league? Will Miami's Darian Mensah have faced tough enough defenses to predict his pro success accurately? Are college defensive coordinators overwhelmingly cracking the code on college quarterbacks more effectively?

The two biggest question marks at quarterback this season stem from Texas quarterback Arch Manning and Oregon quarterback Dante Moore. Manning has proven inconsistent through eight games, including in pivotal moments. Moore's season ended Sept. 26 after he suffered a concussion. Questions on each player weigh their readiness for the NFL and their interest in declaring pro this spring rather than exploring another college year.

Evaluators are split on whether a transfer would help Manning find a better offensive fit. One camp believes that would be the fresh start he needs, while the other believes his family pedigree and résumé will already net him first-round consideration so having just one year to adjust to a new system alongside new teammates could end up hurting his stock more than helping it. Moore, meanwhile, could help his stock if he shows a cleaner bill of health and gets more than his current limited sample size of 19 college starts, evaluators said.

Several quarterbacks are still expected to be drafted in the first round, including the season's biggest riser to this point in Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker. One AFC evaluator said Mestemaker, Notre Dame's CJ Carr and Mensah each would have earned higher evaluations than 2026 first overall pick Fernando Mendoza. Chambliss and Missouri's Austin Simmons intrigue evaluators as well.

Even with mixed reviews on premium positions, including quarterback, a high-ranking AFC executive and a high-ranking NFC executive agreed the draft has more consensus high-end talent than the 2026 class.

"I would say this [year] is maybe a little deeper than last year's in the top 15-20 picks in other positions than quarterback," the high-ranking NFC executive said. "But then after that, it seems like it's a little leaner, and the drafts have been getting a little leaner."

The high-ranking AFC executive credited last year's offensive tackle class and a handful of elite players, like Giants linebacker Arvell Reese. The executive wondered: Are quarterbacks shifting the perception too much?

"The quarterback class, I think people just keep overcorrecting," the executive said. "I think they overcorrected high and now they're overcorrecting all these guys can't play, they'll all stay in school.

"A lot of the sentiment on the draft is driven by what people think about the QBs. But I think even if you take them out, there's some really, really high-end dudes in this draft."

2 paradigms could define teams' trade-deadline value of picks

Evaluators and executives were split on how much the coming draft truly influences teams' trade deadline strategies.

Some evaluators and executives emphasized building a roster is a holistic process that constantly requires a multiyear vision integrating the trade deadline, free agency and draft.

Others believed trade-deadline acquisitions, and their often steep costs, prioritize the current season's outlook. A league source considered teams in three categories .

"There's a team that they're not going to get in the playoffs and so they're doing the best they can to build a winning culture and they're basically playing for next year," the source said of the first group. "Then you have a group of teams that they can get in the playoffs, but they can't win in the playoffs. …

"Then you get teams [that], hey, get in the playoffs and anything can happen."

Expect teams like the Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs and Chicago Bears (Jeffery Simmons already , but perhaps more?) to buy, capitalizing on their already-high ceilings.

Expect teams like the Minnesota Vikings, Pittsburgh Steelers and Seattle Seahawks (like the Bears, they've already started ) to assess whether they can narrow the gap on rosters that simultaneously hold glaring weaknesses and playoff-caliber strengths.

And then expect teams like the Indianapolis Colts ( in progress ), Tennessee Titans (in progress, via Simmons trade) and perhaps even the Las Vegas Raiders to recognize that accumulating assets for next year and beyond is more valuable.

That trifecta should guide teams making bigger swings, the league source said. A high-ranking AFC executive believed there was more nuance involved.

"Honestly, every team in each segment has an argument to make a trade," the executive said. "It's just the level."

Players with potential to meaningfully impact a team beyond 2026 could attract suitors from different competitive stages. Expensive players at depreciating positions (looking at you, Jonathan Taylor) make less sense for teams that aren't contending this season.

Whether teams have a scarcity mindset around draft picks could unfold similarly: Teams like the Titans, New York Jets and Los Angeles Chargers would have little reason to send off their first-round pick as they struggle to win games. But sending a mid-round pick for a player on an expiring deal? Those decisions are more record- and draft class-agnostic, some believe.

"I don't think people care when they trade a third or a fourth," an AFC talent evaluator said. "They look at those as pretty stable resources year over year.

"But I think the teams maybe that are at the top of the draft would maybe consider it because you can kind of anticipate those spots by what's going to be available."

Arguably the most important caveat in any of these decisions: accurately assessing a team's place in its competitive and resource-allocation lifecycle. Trades bust most when teams overestimate their readiness, as the Colts did last year when trading two first-round picks for cornerback Sauce Gardner and the Atlanta Falcons traded back into the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft for edge rusher James Pearce Jr. In contrast, a Bears team that won two of three games even without Caleb Williams this year gave counterparts more confidence in its logic to send two first-rounders for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.

"The teams that do the best job on these trades [are] really understanding what phase you're in and stacking it," the AFC talent evaluator said. "Seattle has a loaded roster and one elite guard really helped them. The Jets have tons of draft capital so acquiring picks makes sense. When you cherry-pick and only do one here and there, I don't think you really get the value or help your franchise long term.

"It's really just a constant balance and a constant push and pull of trying to identify where your team is and what you're going to be in a year or two years because that's where it becomes really valuable."
