articles.title: New Raiders Rumors Reveal Team's Stance on Kirk Cousins Trade Amid Vikings Speculation
articles.summary: ESPN's Adam Schefter isn't buying into speculation that the Minnesota Vikings could look to reunite with Kirk Cousins ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.
articles.body:
ESPN's Adam Schefter isn't buying into speculation that the Minnesota Vikings could look to reunite with Kirk Cousins ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.

"[Cousins] is the perfect mentor to their No. 1 pick who they don't want to rush along, and who they want to leave on the bench... Why are the Raiders trading Kirk Cousins to Minnesota? Why are they doing that?" Schefter asked around the 22:00 mark of Thursday's episode of the Adam Schefter Podcast.

Schefter concluded, "It makes no sense to me."

The Raiders have since gotten off to a 4-4 start behind Cousins, who has completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 2,124 passing yards, with 2026 top pick Fernando Mendoza serving as his backup.

He ranks second in the NFL with 19 touchdown passes with just five interceptions through Week 8.

The Athletic's Michael Silver asked earlier this week if the Vikings could explore a trade for Cousins or the Indianapolis Colts' Daniel Jones in the wake of Kyler Murray's hamstring injury.

"My sense is that nothing has been ruled out," Silver reported.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero said Wednesday on KFAN he felt there was a "low percentage change" the Vikings took a big swing at the trade deadline.

Should the Raiders choose to stick with Cousins to continue pushing for the top of the AFC West while Mendoza continues focusing on his development, the Vikings would have to either seek another quarterback in the next five days or rely on Carson Wentz until Murray is able to return.

Wentz is currently on track to start when the Raiders kick off their Week 9 matchup at the San Francisco 49ers Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Jaguars Overwhelm Lamar Jackson-Less Ravens: 3 Takeaways From Jacksonville's Win
articles.summary: Joe Fagnano never got going against the Jaguars, who delivered a blowout win over the Ravens.
articles.body: No Lamar Jackson. No Snoop Huntley. We didn’t know what to expect back from the Ravens. But we knew there was a chance that it could get ugly Thursday night for Baltimore, which was down to its third-string quarterback in undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano. And it turned out to be exactly that. It was unwatchable. The Jaguars whooped the Ravens 33-10 at M&T Bank Stadium in a game that was never close. Jacksonville (6-2) has recorded back-to-back wins by 20-plus points. Baltimore (4-5) has now lost five straight games. Here are my takeaways: 1.The Jaguars Have At Least One Reason To Be Worried About Their Offense The Jaguars seemed to be playing with fire with the play clock on Thursday night, at least in the first half. On more than a few occasions, it went all the way down to one before they got the snap off. It appeared to hit zero at least a couple of times on the broadcast, though Jacksonville was never penalized for a delay of game. Slow pre-snap development hasn’t been uncommon for the Jaguars this season. Entering this week, they snapped the ball on average with just 7.0 seconds left on the play clock, second-slowest in the NFL, and had used no-huddle just 3.4% of the time, the fourth-lowest, according to Next Gen Stats. Jacksonville runs an efficient offense, to be clear. It entered Week 9 ranked fifth in scoring and 10th in yardage. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence, who’s been playing at a high level since midway through last season, is in complete command at the line of scrimmage. The Jags aren’t a heavily penalized team overall, either (entered Thursday with 55 penalties called against them, 14th-fewest in the league, according to NFLpenalties.com). If communication isn’t clean, though, consistently taking the play clock all the way down to the wire could become an issue late in the season in loud road environments, raising the chances for procedural penalties. It’s not an issue now for the Jags, but it’s something to be wary of moving forward. 2.The Ravens Will Be Thrilled To See Jacoby Brissett With Lamar Jackson and backup quarterback Tyler "Snoop" Huntley out for the Ravens, Fagnano made his first career start for Baltimore and … looked like an undrafted rookie quarterback. It was obvious how much Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle had to simplify and change the offense for Fagnano, who’s significantly less mobile than Jackson and Huntley. Fagnano was kept to half-field reads. Even before the rain started to pour down in Baltimore, making throwing the ball difficult, he didn’t (or couldn’t) push the ball much downfield — he attempted just one pass beyond six yards in the first half. He threw two interceptions deep in Baltimore’s own territory in the second half. The Ravens’ offense looked extremely limited … and bad. Jacoby Brissett, whose trade to Baltimore from the Arizona Cardinals is still to be finalized, doesn’t project to be a game changer who can elevate the Ravens. But he’d give the team competence under center, veteran experience and a passer who can push the ball downfield. And with the weapons the Ravens have on offense, that could be enough to keep the team’s fading playing hopes alive. 3.Jacksonville Might Be The Most Dangerous Team In The AFC This isn’t because of beating up on a Jackson-less Ravens team, but the Jaguars have now won six of their eight games and have a relatively easy second half of the season. Six of Jacksonville’s nine games are against teams that are currently below .500, including its last four games of the season. Currently the No. 4 seed in the AFC, the Jags are in a great position to secure the No. 1 overall seed and the lone first-round bye. And beyond the strength of schedule, the Jaguars are one of the NFL’s most complete teams. They entered Week 9 ranked second in points allowed, first in rushing defense and seventh in pressure rate. They have a Pro Bowl-caliber quarterback and a top-five scoring offense around him. They’re well coached. The Jags don’t get a ton of attention because of the market they’re in, but they are legit and should be on the shortlist of top Super Bowl contenders. 3 ½. What's Next? The Jaguars’ road trip continues for two more games, at the Tennessee Titans (1-7) and the New York Giants (4-2-1), before returning home for a rematch with the Titans on Nov. 29. With Jacoby Brissett entering the fold at quarterback, the Ravens have a winnable stretch of games before their Week 13 bye: vs. the 1-7 Chargers on Monday night in Week 10, at the 3-4 Carolina Panthers (Nov. 22) and at the 2-5 Houston Texans (Nov. 29).

articles.title: NFL Playoff Picture 2026-27, Standings, Bracket Scenarios After Jaguars vs. Ravens
articles.summary: With Week 9 of the NFL season underway, we've officially reached the halfway point in the 2026 campaign, and the playoff picture is starting to come together.
articles.body:
With Week 9 of the NFL season underway, we've officially reached the halfway point in the 2026 campaign, and the playoff picture is starting to come together.

On Thursday, the Jacksonville Jaguars continued their stronghold of the struggling AFC South, improving to 6-2 with a win over the Baltimore Ravens.

The Ravens, meanwhile, dropped to 4-5, and their playoff hopes are dwindling as they continue to be without star quarterback Lamar Jackson.

Ahead of the rest of Week 9 on Sunday and Monday, here's a look at how things are shaking out.

Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2, Lead AFC South)

Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2, Lead AFC North)

Josh Allen and the Bills are in control of both the AFC and the AFC East amid a dominant start to the 2026 campaign, but they can't relax just yet as they try to secure a wild-card bye.

The second half of Buffalo's schedule is relatively daunting, with matchups against the Vikings, Chiefs, Patriots, Bears and more on the way.

The Steelers and Broncos are only a game ahead in their respective divisions, so they can't afford to take their foot off the gas.

The Jaguars are sitting comfortably ahead of the Pack in the AFC South, with the 2-5 Texans sitting in second place. Jacksonville should have no trouble winning its second consecutive division crown.

The race for the division crown is most definitely still on for these four squads.

The Chiefs looked like the team to beat through the first few weeks, but back-to-back losses suggest they're not quite the Super Bowl contenders they appeared to be. Still, any team led by Patrick Mahomes has a shot, and they're just a game back from the Broncos.

The Patriots beat the Bills earlier this season and could very well dethrone them for the AFC East title, and the matchup between those two on Dec. 6 will have plenty of implications.

The Bengals, meanwhile, have looked like playoff contenders; it's just a matter of staying consistent.

The bottom half of the AFC is pretty weak this year, and aside from the Brown, Raiders and Ravens, most of these teams have virtually no chance of reaching the playoffs.

San Francisco 49ers (6-1, Lead NFC West)

The Niners and Vikings are the only two teams in the NFC that have truly looked dominant through the early going. Minnesota's success perhaps comes as a surprise, as it appeared to be in for a rebuilding year, but nonetheless, Kevin O'Connell has his group looking like a contender.

The Giants being atop the NFC East says less about how good they are and more about how bad the rest of the division is. They're the only team above .500 and still have not beaten a team with a winning record.

The same can be said of the Panthers, but they're not far ahead of the Buccaneers and Falcons.

The entirety of the NFC North appears capable of making a Super Bowl run, which makes it arguably the most interesting divisional race to watch. If all four teams reach the playoffs, it would mark NFL history.

The defending champion Seahawks and the new-look Rams both came into the season expecting to compete for a Super Bowl, but injuries have them both off to a rough start. If they can get their rosters healthy, both NFC West squads could turn things around.

The Bucs and Falcons still have a path to the postseason thanks to their weak division, while the Cowboys and Commanders could also both say the same.

articles.title: Ravens were down to their third QB and had a predictably ugly performance in blowout loss to Jaguars
articles.summary: The Ravens had to prepare for Thursday night with their top two QBs on injured reserve.
articles.body: It was sad watching the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday night. The Ravens were a Super Bowl contender not long ago. Many thought they could bounce back from a bad year and be a top team again this season. It's a reason they were scheduled for a prime-time game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 9. But Lamar Jackson got hurt early this season, then got hurt again last Sunday, and Tyler Huntley got hurt too. That left the Ravens to play undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, their third quarterback, on Thursday night. He played through an injured ankle and ended up having to deal with a rainstorm most of the night. He was the Ravens' only option left, and the results were predictable. The Jaguars caught the Ravens at the right time and had an easy night in a 33-10 win. The Ravens finished with 57 yards passing. The Ravens (4-5) have decisions to make before the trade deadline. They are reportedly on the verge of dealing for Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett, and while that will make them a functional offense, it's unlikely Brissett saves the season. Jackson might return from a right thumb injury but that's no guarantee, and the Ravens might be well out of the race by the time he is healed anyway. Thursday night was an uncompetitive, bad game. The Jaguars (6-2) are clearly one of the best teams in the NFL this season, but practically any team would have defeated Baltimore on Thursday night. There wasn't anything the Ravens or Fagnano could do, no matter how many tricks they had in the game plan. It was an unwinnable situation, which might be the case for the rest of their season too. Ravens try to get trickyThe Ravens opened in a wildcat formation with Derrick Henry getting the first snap of the game at quarterback. There were more wildcat plays, extra linemen and any other tricks the Ravens could figure out. Henry even had a pass completion on the first drive. No amount of trickery was saving the Ravens. The Jaguars are a good team with a strong defense and Baltimore couldn't move the ball. The rain didn't help. Baltimore had 27 yards passing in the first half. Its longest completion was 7 yards and its longest play was 9 yards in the first two quarters.Baltimore was trying to stay in it until Jacksonville hit a big play late in the half. Against a blitz, Trevor Lawrence found Parker Washington downfield, and he was in the clear to run for a 50-yard touchdown. Lawrence had 197 passing yards in the first half, more than six times what his counterpart Fagnano had at halftime. Washington's touchdown made the score 17-3. It's hard to count an NFL team out with a half to go, but it was hard to believe Baltimore would score 14 more points, much less outscore Jacksonville by 14. Jaguars pull awayComing out of halftime, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter optimistically told Amazon Prime Video he wanted to see his offense score on the first drive and see what happened after that. The Ravens threw an interception on the first drive. The Ravens were trailing 20-3 when they got a break, as Travis Hunter fumbled and Baltimore recovered near midfield. But the Ravens couldn't get a first down, and on fourth-and-inches tight end Mark Andrews, lined up for what looked like a tush push, fumbled the snap. It looked like he was going to turn and hand it off but it didn't matter because he couldn't hold onto the ball. It was that kind of night. The Jaguars caused some of those issues too. Their defense is very good, and the offense is capable of putting up a lot of points if there's not a downpour of rain. They have a good chance of making a deep playoff run. The same could have been said about the Ravens before Jackson's latest injury. Brissett will be an upgrade over what we saw against the Jaguars, but there was a reason he was demoted to third string by Arizona this week and then was available in a trade. The Ravens' season probably isn't going anywhere. Things could look even worse in Baltimore by Tuesday's trade deadline.

The Jacksonville Jaguars cruised to a 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on Thursday night.

Baltimore was unable to emerge victorious with third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano under center, as starter Lamar Jackson and backup passer Tyler Huntley were both sidelined with injuries .

The Jaguars ended up winning after entering the game as 9.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Jacksonville didn't waste much time jumping out in front on Thursday, opening the game with a 77-yard drive that was capped off by a short touchdown run from Bhayshul Tuten.

The Ravens cut into the early deficit with a 53-yard field goal on their first drive, but the Jaguars quickly pushed their lead back to seven points with a 36-yard field goal of their own.

Baltimore's offense failed to respond for the remainder of the first half, as all three of its possessions in the second quarter ended with punts.

Meanwhile, Jacksonville gained a 17-3 advantage before halftime after Trevor Lawrence connected with Parker Washington for a 50-yard touchdown.

Rainy conditions impacted both offenses during the second half, as the only score of the third quarter was a 45-yard field goal by Jaguars kicker Cam Little.

Little connected on two more field goals to start the fourth quarter before Jacksonville put the finishing touches on the lopsided victory with Chris Rodriguez Jr.'s two-yard rushing touchdown.

Ravens running back Justice Hill immediately responded with a 65-yard score, but a late comeback never materialized.

Baltimore's offense struggled mightily throughout the contest, finishing with just 10 first downs and 227 total yards. The Ravens also committed three turnovers and converted a mere four of 14 opportunities on third down.

Jacksonville maintained its lead atop the AFC South standings by improving to 6-2, while Baltimore dropped to 4-5.

articles.summary: The NFL's Week 9 slate is its last before the 2026 trade deadline on Nov. 10. Organizations across the league will be evaluating their own roster, as well as the 31 other lineups.
articles.body:
The NFL's Week 9 slate is its last before the 2026 trade deadline on Nov. 10. Organizations across the league will be evaluating their own roster, as well as the 31 other lineups.

Case in point, the Baltimore Ravens already made a move by trading for quarterback Jacoby Brissett prior to Thursday's matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars. With Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley injured and Brissett not up to speed, undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano led the Ravens offense. The game went as expected. Baltimore won't be the only franchise dealing with quarterback upheaval this weekend.

Bleacher Report NFL analysts Brent Sobleski , Kris Knox , and Moe Moton will follow all of the weekend's action to break down the biggest stories and ask the most pressing questions coming out of each contest.

Jacksonville Jaguars at Baltimore Ravens

The Jacksonville Jaguars, the Juggernaut

The Jacksonville Jaguars aren't mentioned among the league's elite squads. They need to be. Liam Coen's team may have come up short during their 2025 postseason appearance, but this roster has been outstanding since November of last year.

Thursday's 23-point victory over the Baltimore Ravens became the Jaguars' fourth double digit win this season—which leads the NFL and doubles the league's next-best squad. Furthermore, Jacksonville also has a league-leading eight wins by 20 or more points since the start of the 2025 campaign, according to NFL Researcher .

While the Jags were on the road during their latest outing, Jacksonville has been particularly dominant when playing at EverBank Stadium with seven straight wins by 17 or more points.

Depending on Monday's outcome for the Buffalo Bills, the Jaguars could be tied atop the AFC standings with an opportunity to claim homefield advantage throughout the 2026 postseason.

Will the Jaguars Be Active at the Trade Deadline?

With Thursday's performance, the Jaguars now own a 6-2 record and sit comfortably atop the AFC South. Jacksonville has the potential to be quite active before Tuesday's trade deadline, as a buyer and seller.

To the Jags credit, the league's best run defense slowed Derrick Henry and allowed him to run for only 57 yards. Yes, Justice Hill broke off a 65-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter, but the game was already out of hand. Even so, Jacksonville is in the market for defensive tackle help after DaVon Hamilton suffered a torn quadriceps, according to ESPN's Ian Rapaport .

Furthermore, wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. may be as good as gone. The former 1,000-yard receiver wasn't targeted once during Thursday's contest. He's officially caught one pass during his last four appearances.

Is Joe Fagnano Experience Already Over for Baltimore Ravens?

Joe Fagnano's first start served as a wonderful underdog story of an undrafted rookie who didn't expect to make the Ravens' roster coming out of training camp. He did and was thrust into Baltimore's starting in Week 9 as Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley recover from injuries.

A great story doesn't automatically equate to a fairytale ending. In Fagnano's case, he's likely a one-and-done starter after throwing for 60 yards and two interceptions during Thursday Night Football .

Granted, the wet evening made life more difficult on the first-year quarterback. But it was clear the Ravens weren't going to put the ball in his hands anyway. Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle built the offensive gameplan through Derrick Henry.

Meanwhile, Jacoby Brissett now has 11 days between games to prepare as QB1 after being acquired in a trade from the Arizona Cardinals.

Ravens Experience Another Significant Injury

As if missing a roster's top two quarterbacks isn't enough, the Ravens best defensive player, Kyle Hamilton, left Thursday's contest with a hip injury and didn't return to the game.

Hamilton is a two-time first-team All-Pro. His ability to move around like a chess piece serves as the rudder for the Ravens defense. His 10 tackles for loss/stops at the line of scrimmage are the most among safeties this season, according to Pro Football Focus .

If Hamilton is forced to miss any time, Baltimore's defense will look drastically different.

Sunday's action will be the final indicator of who will be buyers and who will be sellers prior to Tuesday's trade deadline. Though a few have already been determined prior this weekend's matchups. Everyone is looking at you, Indianapolis Colts.

Monday Night Football: Buffalo Bills at Minnesota Vikings

How does an NFL team bench its starting quarterback without calling it a benching? Ask the Minnesota Vikings. Carson Wentz will start Monday against the Buffalo Bills. His inclusion may help since Minnesota continues to struggle offensively. articles.title: 'No Excuses,' Ravens HC Reacts to Blowout Loss to Jaguars After Lamar Jackson Injury
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter wasn't interested in using the absence of star quarterback Lamar Jackson as an excuse for the team's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter wasn't interested in using the absence of star quarterback Lamar Jackson as an excuse for the team's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday.

"Obviously it's a tough situation for our guys," Minter told reporters after the game. "But, I just told them there's no excuses. There's no whatever, we don't have this guy, we don't have that guy. We've got to make a decision again over this break, got a little bit of a break for the guys to mentally reset and come back and seek improvement in all three phases. That's what we'll be after."

With Jackson out due to a right thumb injury and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley sidelined with a toe injury, the Ravens turned to undrafted free agent Joe Fagnano under center.

Fagnano finished 10-of-18 for 60 yards and two interceptions against Jacksonville.

"I'm not here to make excuses," Fagnano said after the game, per Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic. "We just didn't execute. I have to play better."

He was appearing in the second game of his career, as he previously threw for 91 yards while getting picked off once during the Ravens' 36-10 defeat at the hands of the Buffalo Bills on Sunday.

Baltimore's offense was only able to muster three points through three quarters against Jacksonville, finally finding the end zone with a 65-yard rushing touchdown by Justice Hill as the Jaguars held a 33-3 lead in the fourth.

The Ravens picked up just 10 first downs while committing three turnovers during the contest. They averaged 4.2 yards per play.

Baltimore has now lost four consecutive games since opening the season with a 4-1 record.

The Ravens' struggles without Jackson have been particularly disappointing considering the two-time MVP started the year by completing 70.1 percent of his passes for 967 yards and six touchdowns compared to one interception. He also rushed for 144 yards and one score.

Baltimore will now look to bounce back in its next game, a matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 16.

articles.title: ‘Feels Like a No-Brainer,’ ‘Packers Should Call Baltimore’ — NFL World Weighs In on Derrick Henry Trade Rumors After Ravens’ TNF Loss
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens are clearly struggling to keep their season on track, and their latest loss has raised questions about whether Derrick Henry still fits...
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens are clearly struggling to keep their season on track, and their latest loss has raised questions about whether Derrick Henry still fits their plans.

With the trade deadline approaching, the discussion has moved beyond one bad night in Baltimore. NFL insiders and analysts are now weighing whether Henry could finish the season somewhere else.

NFL Insiders React to Derrick Henry Trade Rumors After Ravens' Loss

Baltimore's 33-10 defeat against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night gave trade speculation fresh momentum.

The Ravens fell to 4-5, with Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both on injured reserve. Rookie Joe Fagnano managed just 60 passing yards and threw two interceptions in his first NFL start, leaving Henry without much support from the passing game.

Henry, who ranks 15th in PFN NFL RB Impact , finished with 57 rushing yards on 17 carries. He has failed to reach 60 yards in four consecutive games and is now averaging 3.9 yards per carry, a career low. With his 33rd birthday approaching in January, his timeline may not match Baltimore's uncertain season.

Clay Travis believes the Ravens should consider moving him rather than wasting the remaining years of his career. He posted on X , "The Ravens should trade Derrick Henry to a contender. The season is done, and Henry doesn't have that many years left to play. Feels like a no-brainer."

Pittsburgh Steelers writer Jarrett Bailey also identified a possible destination, suggesting , "The Packers should call Baltimore about Derrick Henry."

The speculation gained more weight when A to Z Sports' Austin Stanley reported interest from two teams. He wrote , "Derrick Henry could be playing his last game with the Baltimore Ravens tonight. Sources tell A to Z Sports that two teams have emerged with serious interest in trading for the future Hall of Fame running back before next week's trade deadline. Keep both eyes open on this one."

Another reporter, John Frascella, posted , "Yeah… Derrick Henry bout to be on a different team."

NFL reporter Justin Ramos also saw a potential deal as a tad more realistic after the loss, writing , "I think right after this game that the Ravens could actually trade Derrick Henry."

Patriots-focused radio host Nick Cattles questioned the financial and roster value of such a move for New England, despite praising Henry's ability. "Derrick Henry is one of the best. But this makes no sense: RB is WAY down the priority list. You have only so many assets to deal after AJB. He turns 33 in January and has a $16.2M cap hit next year. Thanks, but no thanks," Cattles wrote .

Henry's contract could make him an attractive deadline acquisition. His 2026 base salary is just $1.3 million, leaving approximately $650,000 for a new team to pay over the remainder of the season. He is also scheduled to receive $12 million in non-guaranteed compensation in 2027, including an $11 million base salary and a $1 million roster bonus.

The New England Patriots, New York Giants, and Minnesota Vikings have been linked to potential backfield upgrades in reports.

With the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaching, Baltimore must decide whether Henry remains part of its plans or could bring back useful draft capital.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk’s 49ers Comeback Takes Unexpected New Turn
articles.summary: Brandon Aiyuk finally appeared ready to end his standoff with the San Francisco 49ers this week — but him returning might not be that easy. The former All-Pr...
articles.body:
finally appeared ready to end his standoff with the San Francisco 49ers this week — but him returning might not be that easy.

The former All-Pro wide receiver filed for reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list on Wednesday and plans to report to the 49ers' facility on Friday afternoon, agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

"Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field," Rosenhaus said.

It was widely expected to set the stage for his release, which would allow Aiyuk to sign elsewhere. However, there's a $13 million problem standing in the way.

Brandon Aiyuk Could Owe 49ers $13 Million

Aiyuk's push to get released could be complicated by roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture he owes the 49ers, according to NFL Network's Tom Pelissero.

"Veteran WR Brandon Aiyuk owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture — a potential complication in his efforts to secure his release by reporting to the facility Friday," Pelissero posted on X .

"The NFL Management Council and the NFL Players Association are both involved in attempting to resolve the situation. The sides could reach an agreement to pay back the money, or it could go to arbitration. But it's complicated and may take time to resolve."

Aiyuk could simply pay back the money in order to move on and sign with another team. If he elects to try his luck with arbitration, things could drag out for a while.

In other words, showing up on Friday probably won't settle anything.

The 49ers presumably have been eyeing that money for months. NBC Sports Bay Area's Matt Maiocco estimated back in July that the team could claw back anywhere from $13.8 million to $18.4 million of the $23 million signing bonus Aiyuk received in 2024, which is prorated at $4.6 million per year.

"Not only will the 49ers not have to pay him another penny, whereas if he had just shown up, the 49ers would have been on the hook for $27 million for this year, it also enables the 49ers to get a lot of money back," Maiocco said on the "49ers Talk" podcast.

San Francisco has paid Aiyuk $48.1 million since he signed his four-year, $120 million extension in August 2024. He's played seven games since.

Aiyuk hasn't played since tearing his ACL, MCL, and meniscus against the Kansas City Chiefs in October 2024.

Things reached a boiling point during his rehab. The 49ers voided about $27 million in guarantees last summer after Aiyuk failed to meet attendance and rehab requirements.

They then placed him on the reserve/left squad list in December. Since he was on that list when his $24.9 million option bonus for 2026 came due, the 49ers didn't have to pay it.

Aiyuk didn't help his cause this past offseason either. He called out the team in a series of social media posts. He wrote on Instagram in July that he would not be "reinstating with them nor ever doing any kind of business with them."

Head coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch have both said Aiyuk won't play for the 49ers again.

So a release still appears to be the likeliest outcome. Lynch has also said he'd trade Aiyuk to any team that wants him. But previous attempts went nowhere, and the trade deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10.

"I have no expectation," Shanahan said Wednesday when asked about Aiyuk's return, adding he didn't expect a resolution before Friday.

Still, the 49ers have made it clear they're in no rush. They've been content to let Aiyuk sit on the list with zero pay for 11 months, and Pelissero's report suggests they won't let him walk away without getting something back.

So how badly does Aiyuk want to play again?

articles.title: ‘For what?’ – NFL fans can’t believe latest Lamar Jackson contract update
articles.summary: The latest reports about Lamar Jackson’s Ravens future have fans on social media more than a little riled up. Lamar Jackson has been placed on injured reserv...
articles.body:
The latest reports about Lamar Jackson's Ravens future have fans on social media more than a little riled up.

Lamar Jackson has been placed on injured reserve following the injury to his thumb. This has severely impacted the Baltimore Ravens, who are also dealing with an injury to backup QB Tyler Huntley. Another year of big expectations will likely end up in disappointment.

Jackson is no longer a young QB. He is 29 years of age and is supposed to be well in the middle of his prime. However, health issues have become a big narrative over the past couple of seasons. With that in mind, his next contract has become a contentious topic among fans.

Lamar Jackson in line to become NFL's 'highest-paid' star ever and Ravens fans are questioning it

In 2023, Jackson signed a 5-year, $260 million deal with the team. That runs out in 2027, meaning that the team has a big decision to make. Despite his struggles, it would be unexpected if the Ravens chose to move on from Lamar. However, the alternative might be pretty bad too.

According to a recent report from NBC Sports, the team could be on the hook to pay Jackson some big money once again and this time, a lot of fans don't like the idea.

"For what? To sit on the bench for more than half the season?" one fan asked. "And how will you pay for good offensive line to protect him or good wide receivers/tight ends?" another questioned. "This would be the dumbest move I've seen in a while, he's made of glass," a third fan commented.

"The Ravens won't win a Super Bowl with Lamar, so stop wasting everyone's time," a different comment read. "Only way this is working is if they win a ring in 2028 and that's probably not happening," claimed a fifth fan. "I love Lamar but this is a terrible idea," a sixth fan simply said.

Jackson's future is unlikely to lie away from Baltimore, but he has a lot of leverage when it comes to contract negotiations. Despite his recent injury record, QBs like Lamar aren't easy to replace. The Ravens have a massive decision on their hands.

The Green Bay Packers enjoyed a stellar October month which saw them win four of their five matches to bring themselves up to 5-3 for the season. And well, as a result of what has been an impressive season thus far, safety Evan Williams was named NFC Defensive Player of the Month for October after recording 41 tackles, two interceptions, four passes defended, one sack, three quarterback hits and a fumble recovery.

Williams himself credited the red-hot Packers defence for the award , per a post on X by Matt Schneidman.

"Pretty good, pretty good, it's definitely a blessing man, even be considered for something like that," he said. "I feel like it's really more of a group award than anything. We say when we're all succeeding, that's when individuals start to see success … it's a blessing to receive some recognition like that."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Williams was selected in the fourth round of the 2024 NFL draft , and is currently having a breakthrough year. Williams became the third safety since 2000 to record at least 40 tackles and three takeaways in a single month, and the first to accomplish the feat since 2011.

Williams posted a 90.9 overall defensive grade in October, the highest among NFL defenders, while recording 31 solo tackles, six pressures, 10 defensive stops and three turnovers. He allowed just seven completions for 58 yards on targets in coverage, surrendered no touchdowns and gave up a passer rating of 21.1.

Williams received his first Defensive Player of the Month award and became the third Packers safety to win the NFC honor, joining Xavier McKinney in 2024 and Atari Bigby in 2007. Green Bay has now had a player win the October award in three consecutive years, with Micah Parsons receiving it in 2025 and McKinney in 2024.

The Packers will now travel to Gillette Stadium to take on the New England Patriots, and will hope to continue their stellar run in November.

articles.body:
Tom Brady has named Brock Purdy among his MVP candidates after the San Francisco 49ers quarterback impressed during the first half of the NFL season.

Purdy has helped guide the 49ers to a 6-1 record through seven games, despite the team dealing with several injuries on the offensive side of the ball.

The 26-year-old has completed 69.2% of his passes for 1,748 yards, 15 touchdowns and four interceptions. He has also added 161 rushing yards and one touchdown on 32 carries.

Tom Brady backs Brock Purdy's MVP case after impressive San Francisco 49ers start

Brady shared his MVP candidates in his weekly power rankings for Fox Sports, although the NFL legend admitted he was reluctant to make an early prediction.

The former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback named four players who have caught his attention: Purdy, Josh Allen, Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs.

"There's nothing I like less than trying to figure out who's the MVP not even halfway through the season," Brady said.

However, he was particularly impressed by what Purdy has done in San Francisco, highlighting how important the quarterback has been to their winning record.

"Brock Purdy, the 6-1 Niners, I don't think they would be in that position without Brock's steady dependable consistent play. He's done so many great things," Brady added.

Purdy was selected with the final pick of the 2022 NFL Draft, earning the label of 'Mr. Irrelevant'. His performances since entering the league have made that tag look increasingly misplaced.

49ers general manager John Lynch has also praised the quarterback's development, particularly his ability to extend plays and make improvements to his game.

"He's extremely talented," Lynch said. "You see him, the way he goes and extends plays. He's done it in each and every game, aside from being able to stay in the pocket and progress."

Lynch also suggested Purdy had taken criticism about his throwing ability personally, pointing to the improvements he has made in driving the ball downfield.

With Brady now including him in the MVP conversation, Purdy has another endorsement to add to his growing reputation. Maintaining his current production will be important as San Francisco looks to protect its strong start.

articles.title: Ranking the 10 Biggest NFL Trade Deadline Mistakes Over the Last Decade
articles.summary: The Herschel Walker deal between the Dallas Cowboys and Minnesota Vikings is the most infamous trade in NFL history. Ahead of the 1989 NFL trade deadline, the Vikings gave up three first-round picks and three second-round picks as part of their package for the two-time Pro Bowler, which fueled the Cowboys' rise in the 1990s.
articles.body:
The Herschel Walker deal between the Dallas Cowboys and Minnesota Vikings is the most infamous trade in NFL history . Ahead of the 1989 NFL trade deadline, the Vikings gave up three first-round picks and three second-round picks as part of their package for the two-time Pro Bowler, which fueled the Cowboys' rise in the 1990s .

While the Walker trade has stood the test of time as a prime example of how a well-timed deal can help or hurt a franchise, other teams have made tragic mistakes in recent years as the trade deadline approached.

The Vikings learned a hard lesson, which a generation of decision-makers saw as a warning sign. However, those executives no longer populate the league. Instead, today's general managers see opportunities and try to capitalize on them.

"The old-school way of thinking was more anti-trade," one NFC assistant general manager told ESPN's Cameron Wolfe . "Now people are much more open to how they add talent to their teams."

Every trade can be a positive or negative for both sides. But over the last decade, some trade-deadline deals have significantly backfired. Here, we've ranked the worst of the worst.

10. Buffalo Bills Trade for WR Kelvin Benjamin (2017)

Trade : The Buffalo Bills trade 2018 third- and seventh-round picks to the Carolina Panthers for wide receiver Kelvin Benjamin.

During the 2016 campaign and entering the 2017 season, the Buffalo Bills lacked a true No. 1 target. Sammy Watkins dealt with injuries in 2016 and missed half the season. The Bills traded him the following offseason.

Ironically, Buffalo tried to replace him with another offensive weapon who turned out to be damaged goods.

Kelvin Benjamin was 26 at the time of the trade. He posted 1,949 receiving yards during his first two healthy seasons. The Panthers had a glut of wide receivers with upside at the time and decided to move the 2014 first-round pick.

For Buffalo, Benjamin was supposed to be a legitimate X receiver with the size on the outside to consistently create mismatches, particularly in the red zone. However, the version of Benjamin seen earlier in his career never showed up in Buffalo. He caught 39 passes and only two touchdowns in 18 appearances before the Bills released him during the 2018 campaign.

"There's a strong belief that Benjamin hasn't been the same player since he suffered a second knee injury [in 2017], tearing his meniscus in his second game in Buffalo," The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn wrote . "Benjamin missed two games with the injury and then played through it for the rest of the season. He had offseason surgery to repair the injury but never regained his explosiveness.

"Benjamin arrived in Buffalo having already undergone surgery to repair the ACL in his other knee in 2015. The injuries robbed Benjamin of the burst he showed in his 1,000-yard, nine-touchdown rookie season with the Panthers in 2014."

9. Dallas Cowboys Trade for WR Jonathan Mingo (2024)

Trade : The Dallas Cowboys trade a 2025 fourth-round pick to the Carolina Panthers for wide receiver Jonathan Mingo and a seventh-round pick.

The amazing part of the Dallas Cowboys' acquisition of Jonathan Mingo is how little they've received in return even though he's still on the team. To make matters worse, the Kansas City Chiefs flipped a lower draft pick to acquire DeAndre Hopkins prior to the same trade deadline.

"We wanted Mingo when we left [the 2023 NFL draft]," Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said during his weekly radio appearance after making the deal. "We were disappointed we didn't get him. We found out that he could be available. When we found that out, we started a dialogue there. We were looking at a player we had a big interest in when he was coming out. He fits the profile of what we want. He's the type of receiver that is Dak-friendly."

Here's the thing: Mingo hasn't been a "friendly" target for quarterback Dak Prescott. He's caught nine passes in 19 appearances over two-plus seasons. Mingo has started exactly one game during that stretch. He hasn't given the Cowboys anything they envisioned when they made the deal.

Instead, an overreliance on CeeDee Lamb eventually led Dallas to trade for George Pickens, which further pushed Mingo down the depth chart. He and KaVontae Turpin basically flip-flop between the team's fourth and fifth wide receiver options.

8. Baltimore Ravens Trade for Edge Yannick Ngakoue (2020)

Trade : The Baltimore Ravens trade 2021 third-round and 2022 conditional fifth-round picks to the Minnesota Vikings for defensive end Yannick Ngakoue.

After Yannick Ngakoue had a public falling out with Jacksonville Jaguars leadership prior to the 2020 campaign, they traded him to the Minnesota Vikings, where he lasted less than two months before being moved again. Ngakoue finished the season with the Baltimore Ravens, but he did little to elevate their defense.

Ngakoue proved himself as a pure pass-rusher early in his professional career. The 2016 third-round draftee registered 37.5 sacks during his four seasons in Jacksonville. After contract negotiations with the Jaguars broke down, Ngakoue demanded a trade, and the Vikings ponied up. However, the Vikings started the 2020 campaign with a 1-5 record and suffered from buyer's remorse.

The Ravens then added Ngakoue, but they received little in return. The edge-rusher managed only three sacks in 11 total appearances, two of which came in a revenge game against his old team. He provided even less during Baltimore's two postseason outings, with two total pressures.

Ngakoue left in free agency to sign with the Las Vegas Raiders during the following offseason.

Teams That Should Buy at Trade Deadline 🤝

7. Oakland Raiders Trade WR Amari Cooper to Dallas Cowboys (2018)

Trade : The Dallas Cowboys trade a 2019 first-round pick to the Oakland Raiders for wide receiver Amari Cooper.

The Raiders organization hasn't been known for its deft negotiating tactics or drafting. Both bit the franchise when it chose to trade wide receiver Amari Cooper to the Dallas Cowboys prior to the 2018 trade deadline.

The Raiders gave up on the 2015 No. 4 overall pick after seeing a downturn in his production and consistency.

"The production wasn't what it needed to be," Cooper admitted years later . "That's really the only way a team will get rid of you. So I understand. ... I do take responsibility because I did have some drops when I was there. So I do take responsibility for that." However, Cooper rediscovered himself on the Cowboys. He caught 292 passes for 3,893 yards and 27 touchdowns in three-plus seasons with the team. Meanwhile, Hunter Renfrow became the only Raiders wide receiver to post a 1,000-yard campaign during that same stretch. No one else at the position even managed 900 yards.

To make matters worse, the Raiders used the first-round pick they got in return for Cooper to draft safety Johnathan Abram. He spent three-plus seasons with the team, but he got exposed as a one-dimensional safety. The Raiders didn't pick up his fifth-year rookie option and eventually waived him during the 2022 campaign.

6. Houston Texans Trade LT Duane Brown to Seattle Seahawks (2017)

The Trade : The Seattle Seahawks trade 2018 third-round and 2019 second-round picks to the Houston Texans for offensive tackle Duane Brown and a 2018 fifth-round pick.

The Houston Texans thought they were getting a premium return for a declining veteran. They were wrong.

Duane Brown was 32 years old when the Texans shipped him to the Seattle Seahawks. Brown would go on to play seven more seasons, including four and a half in Seattle.

Before the trade, Brown held out in a contentious contract dispute that ended after the first six weeks of the regular season. The offensive lineman even called out Texans owner Bob McNair at the time for what he believed to be were misplaced comments about the team.

Instead of working things out with an excellent performer at a premium position, the Texans sent Brown to the Great Northwest, where he made two Pro Bowls and once earned second-team All-Pro honors.

Without Brown in the lineup, the Texans had a significant roster hole at left tackle. A year-and-a-half later, they made a massive trade to bring in Laremy Tunsil, which cost them a pair of first-round picks and more.

The second of those first-round selections wound up being the third overall pick in the 2021 draft. Kyle Pitts, Ja'Marr Chase, Jaylen Waddle, Penei Sewell, Jaycee Horn, Patrick Surtain II and DeVonta Smith were the seven players chosen directly after that selection.

Tunsil was an excellent player in Houston, but that trade could have been avoided had the Texans had mended fences with Brown, whose career finally ended after the 2023 campaign.

5. New York Giants Trade DL Leonard Williams to Seattle Seahawks (2023)

The Trade : The Seattle Seahawks trade 2024 second- and 2025 fifth-round picks to the New York Giants for defensive lineman Leonard Williams.

Leonard Williams could realistically appear on this list twice as bad deals by the two teams—the New York Jets, then Giants—that eventually jettisoned the defensive lineman. However, Williams' performance with the Seattle Seahawks made the Giants' decision much harder to swallow. The Giants weren't sure whether they could sign Williams to a contract extension going into the 2024 offseason. Plus, they were in a transitional phase under previous head coach Brian Daboll. So Big Blue pulled the trigger on a trade before the 2023 deadline. In retrospect, the Giants didn't get enough in return for Williams, who has been dominant with the Seahawks. Granted, landing second- and fifth-round picks for an expiring contract is usually viewed as an excellent return. In this case, it wasn't. Williams has since been named to two Pro Bowls and a second-team All-Pro. He won a Super Bowl in 2025 as Seattle's best defensive player. Eventually, the Giants also chose to trade Dexter Lawrence. Can anyone guess what position New York will need to address next offseason because it's currently considered a weakness? The defensive interior.

4. Washington Commanders Trade for CB Marshon Lattimore (2024)

The Trade : The Washington Commanders trade 2025 third-, fourth- and sixth-round picks to the New Orleans Saints for cornerback Marshon Lattimore and a 2025 fifth-round selection.

One poor decision created a butterfly effect for the Washington Commanders.

Washington selected cornerback Emmanuel Forbes in the first round of the 2023 draft. By the following season, Forbes was in a rotational role as the Commanders searched for a top corner.

The Commanders acquired Marshon Lattimore before the 2024 trade deadline. They proceeded to release Forbes before the 2024 campaign ended.

Lattimore, who had been named to four Pro Bowls in New Orleans as one of the game's best pure cover corners, was already dealing with a hamstring injury at the time of the deal. He played in only two regular-season games for the Commanders in 2024, although he did participate in their run to the NFC Championship Game.

The veteran cornerback tore his ACL during the following season. Eventually, Washington released him during the 2026 offseason.

In the end, Lattimore played in 14 total games (including postseason) with the Commanders. Even when Lattimore contributed in 2025, Washington still ranked among the league's bottom five in pass defense.

Ironically, the Saints used two picks from the Lattimore deal to select defensive backs who are now regular contributors in their secondary, which is currently ranked higher than the Commanders' in pass defense.

3. Chicago Bears Trade for WR Chase Claypool (2022)

The Trade : The Chicago Bears trade a 2023 second-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers for wide receiver Chase Claypool. Two factors made the Chicago Bears' acquisition of Chase Claypool an awful decision. First, Claypool contributed next to nothing after joining the Bears. He played in 10 games across the 2022 and 2023 campaigns. He caught a total of 18 passes for 191 yards and only one touchdown.

Claypool quickly became disgruntled. The Bears benched him by Week 4 of the 2023 season, then released him midseason.

Second, Chicago paid a hefty price to acquire Claypool.

Technically, the pick it sent to Pittsburgh was a second-round selection. However, it wound up as the 32nd overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft because the Miami Dolphins had to forfeit their first-round selection that year. Chicago could have ended up with a de facto first-round pick, controlled the start of that draft's second day and selected wide receivers Jayden Reed or Rashee Rice, among others. Three years after being released by Chicago, the 28-year-old Claypool is out of the league.

2. Carolina Panthers Trade RB Christian McCaffrey to San Francisco 49ers (2022)

The Trade : The San Francisco 49ers trade 2023 second-, third- and fourth-round picks and a 2024 fifth-round pick to the Carolina Panthers for running back Christian McCaffrey. The Carolina Panthers braced for an inevitable rebuild during the 2022 campaign, and they used their best player to generate as large of a return as possible prior to that season's trade deadline.

Unfortunately, that choice didn't lead the Panthers to more prosperous times. Instead, Christian McCaffrey remains one of the league's top offensive weapons, while Carolina struggles to find any consistency, even in the lowly NFC South. Since being shipped to San Francisco, McCaffrey has generated 3,998 rushing yards, 6,347 yards from scrimmage and 56 total touchdowns in 55 games. He was named the NFL Offensive Player of the Year in 2023 and the NFL Comeback Player of the Year last season while earning first-team All-Pro honors in both campaigns. Meanwhile, the Panthers used some of the draft ammunition they received to trade up for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2023 draft and select Bryce Young. Carolina is 18-40 since choosing Young, with one postseason berth in which the Panthers backed into the playoffs with a losing record and immediately lost in the Wild Card Round.

1. Indianapolis Colts Trade for CB Sauce Gardner (2025)

The Trade : The Indianapolis Colts trade 2026 and 2027 first-round picks plus wide receiver Adonai Mitchell to the New York Jets for cornerback Sauce Gardner.

Initially, the Indianapolis Colts' hyperaggressive approach prior to the 2025 trade deadline made sense. At that point, they had the league's best record even though their defense had struggled. Sauce Gardner was one of the league's best man-coverage corners, was still only 24, and had multiple controllable years left on his current contract.

But since the Colts swung that deal, everything within that organization has become an unmitigated disaster.

Gardner dealt with injuries. Quarterback Daniel Jones suffered a ruptured Achilles tendon. General manager Chris Ballard has been fired. Pro Bowlers Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were traded. Star running back Jonathan Taylor could be next. Overall, Indianapolis has a 3-13 record since trading for Gardner.

Currently, the Colts are in the midst of a lost season. Gardner's presence in the lineup means nothing.

As a final twist, the Colts are on pace to surrender a top-five selection in the 2027 NFL draft, perhaps handing the New York Jets the quarterback whom Indianapolis now needs to jump-start its upcoming rebuild.

articles.title: Top Landing Spots for Ravens' Derrick Henry at 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens are teetering on the brink.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens are teetering on the brink.

A season that started with Super Bowl aspirations is spiraling out of control. The team lost two quarterbacks to major injuries in last week's loss to the Buffalo Bills. The losses are piling up after Thursday's embarrassing home loss to the Jaguars. And as ESPN's Dan Graziano reported, the Ravens now potentially find themselves where few expected a couple of months ago—as sellers at the trade deadline.

And running back Derrick Henry's days in Baltimore could be numbered.

"Henry is turning 33 in January," Graziano said. "He is scheduled to earn $12 million next year, and none of that money is guaranteed. If he isn't in Baltimore's plans beyond this year, the Ravens could find themselves fielding offers over the next week. Henry's base salary this year is just $1.255 million (he made the rest of this year's $14 million via bonuses the Ravens have already paid), so he'd be extremely easy for another team to absorb onto its cap."

Now, it's far from guaranteed Henry will be traded—the Ravens are expected to bring in Jacoby Brissett as a veteran band-aid under center.

But if the team does decide to pull the plug on 2026, there is no shortage of teams who could use the services of the NFL's active rushing leader.

If there's an NFL team that is intimately aware of what Derrick Henry is capable of, it's the Jacksonville Jaguars.

The Jags saw a lot of Henry while he was with the Tennessee Titans, and what they usually saw was him running wild—over 15 career games against Jacksonville, Henry has averaged 5.4 yards per carry, 104.3 rushing yards per game and has found the end zone 16 times on the ground.

The Jaguars are firmly in the driver's seat in the AFC South, and this year's iteration of the team is one of the best in recent memory. The Jaguars have been decent running the ball this season, averaging just under 123 yards per game. Second-year pro Bhayshul Tuten has flashed—he's on pace to top 1,000 yards on the ground this season and has averaged 4.5 yards per carry.

But Tuten is dealing with injuries to his foot and finger, and there's no denying that the addition of Henry would add a new dimension to the Jacksonville offense. With a two-headed run game and all the passing-game weapons the team already has, the jaguars would be a matchup nightmare for opposing defenses.

Jacksonville's Super Bowl window is open. While it is, the team might as well push its chips into the center of the table.

The New England Patriots represented the AFC in Super Bowl LX, and while there have been some bumps in the road this year at 5-3 the Patriots are squarely in the mix once again.

New England's ground game has been solid this season—the Pats are averaging 123.1 yards per game on the ground. But what success the team has had running the ball has been almost entirely the doing of Rhamondre Stevenson—second-year pro TreVeyon Henderson has struggled this year and appears to have fallen from favor.

Even Stevenson has averaged just 3.8 yards per carry, and he has never carried the ball more than 210 times in a season. As Zach McGlone wrote for Chowder and Champions , the addition of Henry would take pressure off of Stevenson—and give New England an intimidating "Thunder and More Thunder" backfield.

"Imagine the Patriots offense drives down the field with some good runs from Stevenson, and then you see The King jogging onto the field in the red zone, and all you can do is pray," he said. "He would be an excellent weapon that could help Drake Maye and would be a nightmare to tackle. At 32 years old, Henry wants a title, and he could be the piece that puts the Patriots over the top and the piece that makes this offense unstoppable in the red zone."

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel already brought in one of his former Titans players in wide receiver A.J. Brown.

It's not especially hard to see why the Denver Broncos have been mentioned as a potential suitor for just about every running back on the market.

The Broncos got a good performance from rookie Jonah Coleman in last week's win over the Kansas City Chiefs. But for the season the Broncos are averaging just 92.6 rushing yards per game—26th in the NFL. JK Dobbins is averaging less than 3.5 yards per carry. RJ Harvey is on injured reserve.

Per Sayre Bedinger of Predominantly Orange , acquiring Derrick Henry would give the Broncos a between-the-tackles presence the team sorely lacks.

"The downhill, no-nonsense running style of Derrick Henry could be exactly what the doctor ordered for the Denver Broncos," Bedinger said. "Henry is now part of a sinking ship with the Baltimore Ravens. Lamar Jackson's latest injury is a season-ender, and his future with the organization beyond this year is now a question mark. Ravens OC Declan Doyle was with the Denver Broncos as recently as 2024 on Sean Payton's staff, and the Ravens were interested in hiring Davis Webb as their head coach this offseason. Henry would only be a short-term rental, but that's all this team really needs in a championship window."

So far this season, the 6-2 Broncos have been able to mostly overcome their offensive deficiencies. But as the team moves deeper into the season and then the playoffs, those deficiencies could be Denver's undoing…

Let's flip to the NFC, because if Henry is dealt it will likely be there.

Among all the postseason contenders listed here, none are more surprised to be there than the Minnesota Vikings. A team that entered the season as a fringe contender at best is tied for the NFC's best record at 6-1.

As Alec Lewis wrote for The Athletic , it puts the Vikings in an interesting spot as the trade deadline nears.

"The Vikings are already punching well above their weight. The only teams spending less cash on their 2026 roster are the Los Angeles Chargers and Miami Dolphins, according to Spotrac. Those teams have a combined 1-13 record. For the Vikings brass, assessing how far to go to supplement this team is an exercise in weighing patience versus aggression. The results will offer perhaps the clearest indication of how (GM Norman) Teasley and the front office view team-building and resource allocation."

Henry isn't a long-term solution in the backfield—he's essentially a one-year rental. But his remaining salary this season is minimal and Minnesota has an extra third-rounder next year that could be used to bring The King to Twin Cities.

It's a win-now move that doesn't carry major ramifications for Minnesota's future. And with the Vikings mired in the middle of the pack at 113.9 rushing yards per game, the team could use the bump in the backfield.

If Minnesota believes they genuinely have a chance at a deep playoff run this year, it's an upgrade that is worth exploring.

At 5-3, the Packers are 1.5 games back of the Minnesota Vikings in the NFC North. If the season ended today, the Pack would be the No. 7 seed in the NFC. The last team in.

In other words, while Green Bay is a good team, it's a good team with little margin for error. And while quarterback Jordan Love is playing at a high level so far this season, the run game has been completely inept. With Josh Jacobs out, the Packers couldn't get anything going on the ground. It hasn't been any better with Jacobs back—he's averaging 2.3 yards per carry, and Green Bay is dead last in the league in rushing at an atrocious 60.6 yards per game.

Yes, Henry isn't having his best season—his 4.0 yards per carry this season is a career-low. And the backs in Green Bay aren't completely to blame for the team's struggles gaining yards on the ground.

But even four yards a pop would be a marked improvement in Titletown—the Packers are averaging less than three yards a carry as a team.

Green Bay doesn't need to be a juggernaut on the ground. But if the team is going to not only make the postseason but do some damage once they get there, the Packers need at least some semblance of offensive balance.

If King Henry really is traded, the New York Giants have to be considered the favorite for his services.

It almost makes too much sense to happen. There's the obvious connection between Henry and Giants head coach John Harbaugh. At 4-2-, the Giants are unexpectedly in first place (by multiple games) in the NFC East. The G-Men are averaging 116.7 rushing yards per game, but there are questions galore at running back—Cam Skattebo is banged up, Tyrone Tracy is on injured reserve and Devin Singletary has all of 18 carries this season.

As Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio said on PFT Live, it's a move that makes sense for all sides involved.

"If you're Derrick Henry, are you showing up today and are you saying 'Please trade me to the Giants', or another contender," Florio said. "If I'm Henry and I'm looking at the calendar and I'm looking at the schedule and I'm looking at the situation and I'm thinking I'm not getting any younger and I'd kinda like to have a playoff run. If I'm the Giants and I'm looking at Jonathan Taylor if I'm John Harbaugh I'm calling my former GM Eric DeCosta today and I'm saying, 'is there any way that Derrick Henry could be available'."

Henry admittedly isn't a long-term solution in the same way that Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall is. Or even Tony Pollard. But Henry also won't be as expensive in a trade as those other backs, and frankly the Giants should be focused on the present.

When you have one playoff appearance over the past decade and you're in first place, you have to live in the now.

articles.title: Updated Panic Meters for Every NFL Team
articles.summary: We've reached that point in the NFL season where panic levels are beginning to rise.
articles.body:
We've reached that point in the NFL season where panic levels are beginning to rise.

Some teams find themselves in contention but are battling obstacles that cause plenty of anxiety, while others are clinging to life on the fringe.

Meanwhile, some have already been put out of their misery, while a few—and it really is just a few—are on cruise control.

Here's a breakdown of where every team stands, on a scale of 1 to 10.

The state of the defense warrants some genuine unease, and the tolerance for anything short of a Super Bowl is extremely low. But the Bills have a relatively comfortable lead in the division and are favored to win it all.

A rebuilding team with limited proven talent has been competitive in every game since Week 3. It was an ugly start but they're overachieving with zero expectations.

To an extent, they're victims of their short- and long-term history. The bar is high. They've flashed plenty of resilience this season and appear well on track to get back to the playoffs, but a deficit in the division and a daunting schedule from here on out have anxiety levels spiking a touch.

The fan base might be beyond panic at this point. I'd imagine most supporters are resigned following a 2-6 start. The panic lies with the dead-man-walking head coach, as well as veterans Geno Smith, Garrett Wilson and Minkah Fitzpatrick.

It can't be higher when you've got Super Bowl expectations but you find yourself in last place and without your franchise quarterback.

As good as the Joe Burrow-led offense has looked of late, it's become apparent that the Bengals will face a tall task trying to overcome defensive liabilities. If they can't, huge changes are likely in store this offseason.

Like the Dolphins, this is a bad team exceeding expectations in a zero-pressure season. It's a small window in which fans can watch without stress before the bar inevitably rises in Year 2 for this regime.

It's not as though they've fallen short of expectations. If anything, they've overperformed. But it's pretty much a constant state of panic when you've got a 42-year-old quarterback and a low margin for error stemming from a lack of overall firepower.

Prior to the season, I figured the panic would surround quarterback C.J. Stroud. Instead, it's a high-panic situation because they're three games back in the division and it has little to do with Stroud. The window is supposed to be wide open, but at 2-5 their season is on the brink.

It's post-panic time now in Indy. They've already dropped their general manager and sold off several key parts. A rebuild looms.

They're cruising, and the window hasn't been open long enough for the expectations to be overwhelming. The only panic realistically relates to mounting injuries on both sides of the ball.

They're uncompetitive with low expectations to begin with, and there should be tolerance for the new staff. That said, Cam Ward's limited improvement is enough to generate some significant anxiety.
